**Department**: Political Science **Salary**: Commensurate with experience
**Description**:


The Department of Political Science at the University of Houston invites applications for two faculty positions in American Politics at the Assistant or Associate Professor ranks to begin Fall 2027\. We seek applicants whose research and teaching interests focus broadly on American Politics and are open to specialty.
  

  

The American Politics subfield at the University of Houston boasts scholars with a wide range of interests, including political behavior, institutions, and public policy. Special consideration will be given to those whose research agendas will add to the department’s existing strengths in this subfield and have potential for collaboration with a variety of current faculty. Successful candidates should have extensive methodological training, demonstrated excellence in scholarly research and publication, and a clear commitment to teaching.
  

  

Salary and rank commensurate with experience. Applicants much have a PhD in Political Science. Appointments at the tenured Associate Professor rank must have a record of research, teaching, and service consistent with the bylaws of the Department of Political Science for promotion to associate professor with tenure. Review of applications will begin October 1 and continue until the position is filled.
  

  

The University of Houston, a dynamic research institution founded in 1927, stands as a vibrant hub of academic excellence in Texas. With over 49,000 students, it offers a comprehensive range of programs across 15 colleges, fostering innovation in fields such as energy, health, hospitality, business, education, law, STEM, and the humanities. Boasting top\-tier faculty, state\-of\-the\-art facilities, student success initiatives, and a strong commitment to community engagement, UH prepares students to thrive in a globally interconnected world while contributing impactful research and innovation to the region and beyond.
  

  

The Department of Political Science provides high\-quality undergraduate and graduate education, with over 800 majors and 75 M.A. and Ph.D. students. The Department capitalizes on the strengths of our city, offering students and faculty opportunities to research the politics of the future in a dynamic hub of international commerce, and in a region that is on the leading edge of national demographic and economic trends.
  

  

The University's prime location in America's fourth\-largest city supports extensive industry partnerships and experiential learning opportunities. Renowned for its energy industry and NASA's Space Center, Houston is home to a vibrant scene with world\-class museums, theaters, and restaurants. Houston thrives as a hub for innovation, education, and arts, fostering a unique blend of community charm and modern progress.
  

  

Applications should be submitted through the University’s online job site, http://www.uh.edu/human\-resources/uh\-careers/. The position number keyword is 496784\. To apply please submit a letter of application, CV, short writing sample, unofficial transcripts, and contact information for three professional references. Listed references will be asked to provide letters of recommendation for junior candidates only.
  

  

For further information please contact Professor Brandon Rottinghaus at bjrottin@central.uh.edu.  

  

  



Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of Texas for the duration of their appointments.
  

  

Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
  

  

All positions at the University of Houston\-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e., communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems, electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the security and integrity of the research is maintained.
  

  

The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

### **Application Deadline:**


Review of applications will begin on October 21, 2026\.


### **Position Details:**


This full\-time faculty position is on\-campus and in\-person.
  

  

The Department of Strategic Communication in the Bob Schieffer College of Communication at Texas Christian University (TCU) in Fort Worth, Texas invites applications for a full\-time tenure\-track Assistant Professor to begin in August 2027\. We seek candidates whose research and teaching contribute to the field of strategic communication and expand the department’s strengths. The department has particular interest in candidates with qualitative approaches to strategic communication. We seek candidates whose research contributes to areas of disciplinary relevance and student demand, including: advertising and brand communication; sports communication; social and cultural implications of strategic communication; technology and society; digital, social, and emerging media.
  

  

Applicants must be able to teach a variety of introductory and upper\-level undergraduate and graduate courses in our program, including, for example; introductory advertising or public relations, creative strategy, management, research, global communication, law and/or ethics, campaigns, or other required courses. Candidates may have an interest in creating and teaching new electives. Successful candidates may also benefit from the Schieffer Media Insights Lab, which is the college’s social and digital media research and teaching facility, and have the opportunity to contribute to our college\-level PhD in Media and Communication or our postbaccalaureate certificate program in digital and social media analysis.
  

  

Required qualifications:
  

  

Ph.D. in a relevant field (e.g., advertising, public relations, strategic communication, communication, marketing, consumer psychology) by the time of appointment;
  

  

Evidence of research productivity or a developing research agenda with potential for publication in high\-impact scholarly outlets in the advertising, public relations, and/or strategic communication disciplines;
  

  

Demonstrated commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring;
  

  

Ability to contribute to a collaborative and collegial academic environment.
  

  

Preferred qualifications:
  

  

Expertise in strategic communication, including but not limited to brand communication, consumer culture, digital advertising, creative strategy, persuasion, and other related areas;
  

  

Expertise in qualitative research methodologies, such as in\-depth interviewing, ethnography, discourse analysis, netnography, interpretive consumer research, critical\-cultural approaches, or mixed\-methods designs that incorporate qualitative inquiry;
  

  

Evidence of a research agenda with relevance to contemporary strategic communication issues affecting consumers, organizations, communities, or society;
  

  

Related professional experience and strong relationships with strategic communication industries are highly desirable.
  

  

We seek candidates who are committed to providing undergraduate and graduate students with an active, supportive learning environment, advancing knowledge through theoretically and practically significant scholarship, and contributing to the inclusive excellence of our university community.
  

  

The teaching load for tenure\-stream faculty is 2\-3 or 3\-2, with course reductions offered in the first year and fourth year to support their progress toward tenure and promotion.


### **Department Details:**


The Department of Strategic Communication is TCU's home for advertising, public relations, and new media. Through the theories, methods, and practices of strategic communication taught by highly regarded teachers, scholars, and professionals, students learn to create effective, innovative, and responsible stories about brands and organizations, solving real\-world communication challenges. The Department of Strategic Communication is one of four departments in the Bob Schieffer College of Communication, housed in the Moudy South Building, and serves more than 400 majors. In addition to state\-of\-the\-art facilities, which include writeable walls, updated classroom and computer technology, and adaptable furniture, the Department of Strategic Communication also has cutting\-edge educational experiences from the student\-run strategic communication agency, Roxo, to the National Student Advertising Competition (NSAC) and guided internships.


### **School/College Description:**


In 2023, the Schieffer College celebrated the 10th anniversary of its naming for TCU alumnus and longtime CBS network TV correspondent Bob Schieffer. The college is the academic home for four departments: Communication Studies; Film, Television, and Digital Media; Journalism; and Strategic Communication. Some 1,150 undergraduate student majors complete coursework in areas that include: Advertising and Public Relations; Cinema and Media Studies; Digital and Social Media; Health Communication and Media; Interpersonal and Organizational Communication; Journalism and News Media Studies; and Sports Broadcasting. About 30 graduate students pursue master’s degrees in Communication Studies or Strategic Communication, and some 60 full\-time and 15 part\-time faculty teach in the college. The college’s award\-winning student experiential learning activities include print, video, and digital news media, a speech and debate team, an advertising and public relations agency, a radio station, and sports broadcasting productions. The college also offers a number of off\-campus study options to students.


### **University \& Fort Worth Description:**


About TCU
  

  

Founded in 1873, Texas Christian University is a world\-class, private, Carnegie\-classified national research university located in Fort Worth, Texas. Inspired by its mission and core values of integrity, engagement, community, and excellence, TCU consistently ranks among the top universities and colleges in the United States.
  

  

TCU’s campus — regularly ranked among the nation’s most beautiful — spans 302 acres in a primarily residential area just minutes from downtown.
  

  

The university comprises nine schools and colleges offering 117 areas of undergraduate study, 62 master’s level programs, and 37 areas of doctoral study. TCU is a leader across several disciplines, including health care, business, energy, and the arts. Total enrollment stands at 12,980, including 11,152 undergraduates and 1,828 graduate students. Students are supported by over 2,200 faculty and staff, including more than 700 full\-time faculty members.
  

  

About Fort Worth
  

  

Fort Worth blends the approachable charm of a smaller city with the amenities, cultural energy, and distinctive personality of a major metro. As the nation’s 11th\-largest city, with a rapidly growing population of more than 1 million, Fort Worth and TCU share a relationship that spans more than a century — one that continues to deepen as many Horned Frogs choose to stay after graduation, drawn by the region’s thriving job market. Part of the Dallas\-Fort Worth metropolitan area — the nation’s fourth\-largest and a top tourism destination — Fort Worth earned recognition from U.S. News \& World Report in 2025 as the No. 4 best big city to live in the United States.
  

  

Fort Worth offers an impressive array of cultural, educational, and entertainment opportunities, anchored by three world\-class art museums — the Kimbell Art Museum, the Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth, and the Amon Carter Museum of American Art. The Bass Performance Hall stands as one of the premier performance venues in the country. Throughout the year, residents and visitors alike enjoy concerts, film festivals, and other cultural events at Sundance Square, Dickies Arena, Panther Island, and Near Southside venues.


### **Required Application Materials \& Application Instructions:**


Applications must include a cover letter that addresses the position requirements, curriculum vitae, statement of teaching philosophy, evidence of teaching effectiveness, and a list of three academic references with current contact information included. Applications must be submitted electronically through the TCU HR system.


Letters of recommendation will be requested from your three references at a later stage in the process. Your references will receive an email from TCU asking them to upload their LOR on your behalf.


### **Employment Values Statement:**


Texas Christian University values Integrity, Engagement, Community, and Excellence in the workplace. TCU treats applicants and employees with fairness and respect. TCU hires and promotes individuals based on their qualifications and their commitment to making a positive impact on our student\-centered community. TCU is an equal opportunity employer and follows all applicable employment laws. TCU fairly considers all qualified individuals, ensuring we are a workplace free from unlawful discrimination and harassment.


### **TCU Annual Security Report \& Fire Safety Report Notice of Availability**


Texas Christian University is committed to assisting all members of the campus community in providing for their own safety and security. TCU’s Annual Security Report and Fire Safety Report is published in compliance with the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy \& Campus Crime Statistics Act (Clery Act) and the Higher Education Opportunity Act. This report includes statistics for the previous three calendar years concerning reported crimes that occurred on campus, in certain off\-campus buildings owned or controlled by the University, and on public property within, or immediately adjacent to and accessible from the campus. The statements of policy contained within this report address institutional policies, procedures, and programs concerning campus security, alcohol and drug use, crime prevention, the reporting of crimes, emergency notifications and timely warning of crimes, sexual and interpersonal violence, and personal safety at TCU. Additionally, this report outlines fire safety systems, policies and procedures for on\-campus housing facilities, as well as residence hall fire statistics.


The Annual Security Report and Fire Safety Report can be found on the TCU Police Department website at https://police.tcu.edu/annual\-security\-report, or a paper copy of the report may be obtained by contacting the TCU Police Department at 817\-257\-7930, or via email at police@tcu.edu.

jobs.description:
UNC Charlotte is a Carnegie R1 research university located in one of the nation’s fastest growing major metropolitan areas. The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at UNC Charlotte serves approximately 600 undergraduate students and 75 graduate students, offering B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. degrees in Civil Engineering, as well as a B.S. degree in Environmental Engineering. The CEE Department currently comprises 25 full\-time faculty members who are actively engaged in research and teaching across geotechnical, geoenvironmental, environmental, water resources, structural, and transportation engineering. The faculty value student\-faculty engagement, excellent undergraduate and graduate instruction, and a collaborative, supportive research culture. The department is housed in EPIC, a 200,000\-square\-foot engineering research and academic facility that provides exceptional laboratories and teaching spaces. Additional information about the department is available at**https://cee.charlotte.edu**.
  

**Vacancy Open to** All Candidates
  

**Description of Work**
The University of North Carolina at Charlotte recognizes the differentiation of mission, goals, and objectives inherent in the diversity of disciplines represented by its colleges and departments. Thus, the Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure Track Faculty should be interpreted in the context of the related departmental and collegiate goals.
  

Teaching, Advising, Curriculum and Instructional Development – Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to teaching may include but are not limited to: subject matter competence, course design, course presentation, advising and consultation, directing student research, curriculum and instructional development, and grading student work.
  

Scholarly Research, Creative, and Other Professional Activities – All tenured and tenure\-track faculty are expected to participate in expanding the knowledge base of their academic field by conducting research or engaging in other creative activities as appropriate to the faculty member’s discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to research may include but are not limited to: research/creative activity that generates new knowledge and/or synthesizes and/or integrates existing knowledge, publication, an on\-going agenda for research, scholarly, and creative activity, and are expected to seek extramural support for their work.
  

Service to University, the Public, and the Profession – All tenured and tenure\-track faculty are expected to engage in a program of service appropriate to their discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to service may include but are not limited to: service to the administration and governance of the University, public service, and service to the profession.
  

  

This position is subject to research\-security screening. As part of the application, applicants must disclose, **either in their CV or in a separate document submitted with the application**, all current appointments or affiliations with foreign institutions or organizations, foreign research support, and ongoing research collaborations with foreign institutions, organizations, or their personnel. Before candidates advance to an on\-campus interview, the university will review this information and other publicly available information for relationships involving institutions on the current Section 1286 list and any other applicable U.S. restricted\-party lists. A disclosed or identified relationship does not automatically disqualify a candidate. As a condition of employment, a selected candidate must resolve any relationship the university determines would violate applicable law or sponsor requirements or materially impair the candidate’s or the university’s eligibility for federal funding.
  

  

To view the complete Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure\-Track Faculty document visit our website: https://facultyhandbooks.charlotte.edu/full\-time\-faculty\-handbook/
  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte (UNC Charlotte) invites applications for a tenure\-track Assistant Professor position in Geotechnical Engineering. The search is open to candidates from all areas of geotechnical engineering, with particular interest in fundamental and experimental soil mechanics; foundation engineering and soil\-structure interaction; geosynthetics and sustainable geomaterials; underground construction and rock mechanics; geoenvironmental engineering; transportation and aviation geotechnics; defense/energy geotechnics and infrastructure; and infrastructure resilience. Candidates who integrate advanced computational geomechanics, large\-scale or field experimentation, artificial intelligence and data science, or advanced sensing and monitoring into these or related areas are particularly encouraged to apply. Outstanding candidates across allother emerging sub\-disciplines of geotechnical engineering are also invited to submit applications. The anticipated start date for the position is August 11, 2027\.  

  

  

The successful candidate will strengthen and expand the Department’s existing geotechnical expertise, foster interdisciplinary research collaborations, and contribute to the growth of its research and graduate programs. The candidate will be expected to leverage relevant research facilities and engage with College research centers and institutes, as appropriate to their research program, including the Energy Production and Infrastructure Center (EPIC), the National Defense \& Intelligence Innovation Institute (NDI3\) and the Charlotte Aviation Innovation and Research (AIR) Institute. The Department provides access to state\-of\-the\-art teaching, laboratory, and research facilities, including the EPIC\-High\-Bay Structural Laboratory, which offers extensive capabilities for large\-scale structural and geotechnical testing, advanced sensing, and experimental research supported by dedicated technical staff.
  

**Essential Duties:** Candidates will be responsible for:
* Developing and maintaining a strong, sponsored research program, including publishing high\-quality research in peer\-reviewed journals.


* Contributing to undergraduate and graduate curricula through core and elective courses in geotechnical and/or geoenvironmental engineering, as well as developing new courses aligned with infrastructure systems and emerging trends.


* Mentoring and advising graduate students and research assistants.


* Engaging in departmental, university, and professional service.


* Fostering interdisciplinary partnerships within the university and externally with stakeholders in government, industry, and non\-profit sectors.


  

**Minimum Experience/Education**
UNC Charlotte gives primary consideration to the earned doctorate or terminal degree in the teaching discipline or a related discipline.
  

**Preferred Education, Skills and Experience**
* Minimum education required is a Ph.D. in Civil Engineering or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
* Expertise in geotechnical engineering with particular interest in fundamental and experimental soil mechanics; foundation engineering and soil\-structure interaction; geosynthetics and sustainable geomaterials; underground construction and rock mechanics; geoenvironmental engineering; transportation and aviation geotechnics; defense/energy geotechnics and infrastructure; and infrastructure resilience
  
  

  

**Necessary Licenses/Certifications**
While not required, candidates with a Professional Engineering (PE) license, or willingness to obtain one, are particularly encouraged to apply.  

  

  

  

**Special Notes to Applicants**
The University of North Carolina at Charlotte is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against employees or applicants for employment based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, physical or mental disability, veteran status, or any other protected status. In keeping with this commitment, UNC Charlotte ensures that persons of any background are invited, included, and treated equally in the terms and conditions of employment. Finalists will be subject to a criminal background check.
  

  

Applications for Position \#004625 must be submitted electronically at https://jobs.charlotte.edu and must include:
* A cover letter articulating how your qualifications and experience make you a viable candidate for this tenure\-track Assistant Professor appointment.


* A comprehensive curriculum vitae.


* A combined statement of research, teaching, and leadership vision.


* A list of three professional references who can attest to your academic experience and technical expertise.


All requested documentation must be submitted for an application to be considered. Review of applications will commence on December 15, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.

About Sacred Heart University
  
  

As one of the nation’s largest Catholic universities and among the fastest\-growing private doctoral institutions in the U.S., Sacred Heart University is a national leader in shaping higher education for the 21st century. SHU offers more than 100 undergraduate, graduate and doctoral programs on its Fairfield, Conn., campus. Sacred Heart also has a campus in Dingle, Ireland, and offers online programs. Nearly 10,000 students attend the University’s nine colleges and schools: College of Arts \& Sciences; School of Communication, Media \& the Arts; School of Social Work; School of Computing \& Engineering; School of Performing Arts; College of Health Professions; the Isabelle Farrington College of Education \& Human Development; the Jack Welch College of Business \& Technology; and the Dr. Susan L. Davis, RN, \& Richard J. Henley College of Nursing. Sacred Heart, a Laudato Si’ campus, stands out from other Catholic universities as it was established to be led by the laity. This contemporary Catholic university is rooted in the rich Catholic intellectual tradition and the liberal arts and, at the same time, cultivates students to be forward thinkers who enact change in their own lives, professions, and communities. Sacred Heart University has earned national recognition for academic excellence, student success, career outcomes, and campus experience. The Princeton Review recognized SHU in its Best 392 Colleges: 2027 Edition and Best Business Schools: 2027 Edition, while additional national recognitions highlight the University’s commitment to preparing students for meaningful careers and lifelong success. Sacred Heart is home to the award\-winning, NPR\-affiliate station, WSHU Public Radio; Division I athletics; and an impressive performing arts program that includes choir, band, dance, and theatre. www.sacredheart.edu
  
  

View SHU’s Faculty Experts Here
  
  

Sacred Heart University (SHU), located in Fairfield, Connecticut, houses its School of Computing \& Engineering (SCE) within the College of Arts \& Sciences. SCE offers two graduate programs (M.S. in Computer Science \& Information Technology and M.S. in Cybersecurity), and seven undergraduate Bachelor of Science programs—Computer Science, Information Technology, Game Design \& Development, Cybersecurity, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering.
  
To support the continued growth of its computing programs, the School of Computing and Engineering invites applications for a tenure\-track Assistant Professor for the ABET\-accredited B.S. in Computer Science program at SHU. The successful candidate will be a dynamic and innovative educator\-scholar committed to excellence in undergraduate teaching, student mentoring, and scholarly activity. The position emphasizes hands\-on, project\-based learning and active engagement with students, while contributing to curriculum development and continuous program improvement aligned with ABET accreditation standards. The anticipated start date for this position is August 2027 (Fall semester).
  
  

**Primary responsibilities include:**  

* Designing and teaching problem\-based, hands\-on undergraduate courses in computer science, with an emphasis on machine learning, generative AI, natural language processing, and computer vision.
* Conducting scholarly computer science and artificial intelligence research appropriate for a teaching\-focused institution.
* Supervising graduate and undergraduate student research as well as mentoring senior capstone design projects.
* Collaborating with industry partners and the SHU community on interdisciplinary projects.
* Supporting continuous program improvement and ABET accreditation activities.


**Minimum Qualifications:**  

* Ph.D. in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence or a closely related discipline, completed by the start date of the appointment.
* Expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning and language models preferred.
* Commitment to a highly interactive, student\-centered learning environment
* Openness to innovative and hands\-on pedagogical approaches
* Demonstrated potential for scholarly research and professional growth
* Experience developing or maintaining industry collaborations


**Preferred Qualifications:**  

* Experience with active or project\-based learning approaches
* Experience applying machine learning techniques within any scientific context
* Evidence of an ongoing scholarly research agenda and publication activity
* Experience developing or maintaining industry collaborations


**To apply, please submit the following materials:**  

* A cover letter describing your interest in the position and how your background aligns with the responsibilities and qualifications
* A curriculum vitae

jobs.description:
##### **Description**


The Department of Engineering Technology and Industrial Distribution, College of Engineering at Texas A\&M University invites applications for a full\-time tenure\-track position at the assistant professor level with a 9\-month academic appointment, and the possibility of an additional summer appointment contingent upon need and availability of funds, beginning in Fall 2027\. The successful applicant will be required to teach; advise and mentor graduate students; develop an independent, externally funded research program; participate in all aspects of the department's activities; and serve the University, College, Department and profession.


The successful candidate will have opportunities to pursue courtesy appointments in other departments within the College of Engineering, such as Electrical and Computer Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, and Industrial and Systems Engineering. Many Engineering Technology and Industrial Distribution faculty members hold courtesy appointments across the College, reflecting a tradition of cutting\-edge research and interdisciplinary collaboration. Such appointments are subject to approval by the departments and university and graduate program policies. Once a courtesy appointment is approved, the faculty member will be eligible to recruit graduate students, including M.S. and Ph.D. students, from courtesy department(s) and serve as their primary advisor, subject to the policies of the respective graduate program.


**Department Info:**  

The Department of Engineering Technology and Industrial Distribution is unique among the many departments within the College of Engineering, due to its strong focus on applied research and undergraduate education. The Engineering Technology and Industrial Distribution Department blends engineering and business knowledge, methods, and research. This department consists of four distinct undergraduate programs and three graduate programs \- two distance education and one resident graduate program. Minors in Embedded Systems Integration, Technical Sales, and Information Technology Services Management are also available. More information available here: (https://engineering.tamu.edu/etid/index.html)


As the largest in student enrollment (\~2600 undergraduate and over 230 graduate students) in the college, the department has 116 faculty members, including 40 tenured/tenure\-track and 76 full and part\-time academic professional track faculty members to support academic programs in electronic systems engineering technology, multidisciplinary engineering technology, manufacturing and mechanical engineering technology, information technology service management, and industrial distribution. Department research expenditures exceed $12 million annually supporting areas such as embedded systems, communications, advanced manufacturing, intelligent product design and development, information technology management, human\-computer interaction, robotics and automation, sales management, distribution operations and supply chain management (led by the Thomas and Joan Read Center for Distribution Research and Education), engineering education and workforce development. In addition to the programs on the College Station campus, the department also has remote programs on branch campus sites.


**University/College Info:**  

Texas A\&M University lies in the heart of the Texas Triangle, a dynamic region anchored by Dallas\-Fort Worth, Houston, and Austin\-San Antonio. Nestled within the twin cities of Bryan and College Station, with a metro population exceeding 287,000, it thrives at the core of this economic and cultural hub. Texas A\&M is one of the largest public universities in the nation, and one of the few to have land\-, sea\- and space\-grant designations. Boasting a large student body, Texas A\&M University has more than 81,000 graduate and undergraduate students enrolled across all campuses, with over 74,000 based in College Station. Supported by robust financial resources, the Texas A\&M University System and related foundations reported a Fiscal Year (FY) 2025 endowment valued at more than $22 billion, ranking 8th overall and 2nd among public institutions (as reported by the National Association of College and University Business Officers). Demonstrating research excellence, Texas A\&M University in College Station and its Health Science Center achieved research \& development expenditures of nearly $1\.4 billion for FY2024, as reported in the National Science Foundation’s Higher Education Research and Development Survey, placing Texas A\&M among the top 25 institutions nationwide. Leading in engineering education, the College of Engineering, with more than 830 faculty members and over 24,000 students, is one of the largest engineering schools in the country. Recognized for academic excellence, the college’s undergraduate and graduate programs are ranked in the top 10 among public institutions by U.S. News \& World Report, with several departments ranked in the Top 10\. Additionally, topping engineering research, the college is ranked first in engineering research expenditures by the American Society for Engineering Education.

jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science at Tulane University invites applications for a Professor of Practice position beginning in Fall 2027\. We welcome and encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups. Our friendly, collaborative, and collegial department currently has 14 tenure\-track/tenured faculty and four Professors of Practice, with a commitment to continue to grow over the next few years. In our research and teaching, we take pride in our equal focus on both computer science and its interdisciplinary applications. Our current faculty are engaged in collaborative research with colleagues in the School of Science and Engineering, the School of Liberal Arts, and the Health Sciences, and our faculty are at the forefront of Artificial Intelligence research and AI initiatives throughout campus. More information about the department, its faculty, its research areas, and its undergraduate and graduate programs can be found at https://sse.tulane.edu/cs .


The department is looking to expand its expertise in computer systems and programming languages. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, programming languages and compilers, cybersecurity, databases, distributed systems, and operating systems. Outstanding candidates from other areas will be considered as well. The successful candidate will have a record of excellent teaching and mentoring at the undergraduate level, a commitment to student\-centered teaching, and a drive to support our students both in and out of the classroom.


The School of Science and Engineering provides exceptional opportunities for collaboration across disciplines and supports the development of cutting\-edge research and educational initiatives. The School is distinctive as the only academic unit at a major research university to merge the behavioral sciences, physical sciences, life sciences, engineering, and mathematics, which provides an unusually rich environment for innovative programs and interdisciplinary research.


Tulane University is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is classified by the Carnegie Foundation as an R1 (Very High Research Activity) and Community Engaged university. Tulane brings together bold and creative scholars, scientists, and students who are committed to crossing boundaries. Data\-intensive discovery lies at the heart of research and education at Tulane and is fueled by Tulane’s Jurist Center for Artificial Intelligence , the Center for Community\-Engaged Artificial Intelligence , and the Connolly Alexander Institute for Data Science . Tulane resides in historic New Orleans, Louisiana – a city that takes the utmost pride in its vibrant music scene, world\-class restaurants, rich confluence of cultures and traditions, and festive Mardi Gras parades. "The things that make life worth living – eating, drinking and the making of merriment – are the air that New Orleans breathes." \- Adam Karlin, Lonely Planet. **Job Summary**
---------------

The College of Science at Purdue University invites applications for a tenure\-track faculty position in Actuarial Science at the assistant or associate professor level, based at Purdue’s Indianapolis campus. Purdue’s Actuarial Science program, jointly administered by the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics, is nationally recognized for excellence in actuarial education. This position is part of an initiative to expand the program to the Indianapolis campus, including the recruitment of additional instructional faculty to support and advance the program’s teaching mission.  



  

Purdue University in Indianapolis is a new, fully integrated expansion of the West Lafayette campus, extending to central Indiana the academic rigor and accessible excellence for which Purdue is known. As the state’s only public top\-10 university, most trusted university, and most innovative university, Purdue is focused on strengthening its presence in Indiana’s industrial and technological center. Purdue in Indianapolis is creating an innovative, STEM\-based collegiate experience by connecting future\-ready students and faculty with local businesses to accelerate Indiana’s STEM pipeline and technology ecosystem, fueling impact for our region and the world. Learn more about Purdue’s latest giant leap at: https://www.purdue.edu/campuses/indianapolis/ .  



Qualifications
  

Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, or a closely related field by August 16, 2027, and have demonstrated excellence in research and a strong commitment to teaching. Outstanding applicants in all areas of actuarial science will be considered, including, but not limited to, probability, risk measurement, stochastic modeling, data science, and the broader mathematical and computational sciences. Preference will be given to candidates who are willing to acquire experience with, or who already have experience with, the examination system that governs the actuarial profession.  



Principal Duties
  

Successful candidates will be expected to develop research programs in their fields of expertise, teach courses in actuarial science, develop an external funding portfolio, build connections with the actuarial profession, and participate in the program, college, and broader university activities.  



The Program and College
  

Purdue’s Actuarial Science program is recognized as a Center of Actuarial Excellence by the Society of Actuaries. The program offers a stimulating academic environment that connects research areas with the actuarial profession. With over 300 undergraduate students and a thriving partnership with Purdue’s Data Mine learning community, the program is also tightly coupled with some of Purdue’s fastest\-growing majors, such as Data Science.  



  

Actuarial Science is part of the College of Science, which encompasses the mathematical, computational, physical, and life sciences at Purdue. The College is the second\-largest at Purdue with over 350 faculty members and more than 7,000 students. The College is pursuing significant new initiatives that align with campus\-wide plans, with data science among its strategic priorities. Opportunities for collaboration span mathematics, probability, statistics, the physical and life sciences, as well as the newly reimagined School of Business and Purdue’s burgeoning campus presence in the center of Indianapolis.  



  

For more information about Purdue’s Actuarial Science program, see https://www.science.purdue.edu/actuarial\-science/ .


**Application Procedure**
-------------------------

Applications should be submitted online through www.mathjobs.org and should include (1\) a cover letter, (2\) a curriculum vitae, (3\) a research statement, (4\) a teaching statement, and (5\) four letters of recommendation, one of which should address the candidate’s teaching qualifications. Reference letter writers should submit their letters online through www.mathjobs.org . Inquiries may be directed to Dr. Haibo Liu at haiboliu@purdue.edu. Applications will be considered on a continuing basis, but candidates are encouraged to apply by January 10, 2027, for full consideration.  



A background check will be required for employment in this position.

The Department of Chemistry at Tufts University invites applications for a full\-time, non\-tenure\-track faculty position as Professor of the Practice. The successful candidate will provide strategic and academic leadership for the Department’s Master’s programs while also playing a central role in preparing students for careers in the chemical sciences by connecting rigorous academic training with the skills and experiences needed for success in industrial, academic, and other professional settings. This role focuses on leadership of the Department’s Master’s programs, graduate education, mentorship and career development for our students, and building connections between the Department, industry and other external partners.


Through combined leadership, teaching, mentoring, and external\-engagement responsibilities, the Professor of the Practice will play a critical role in the Tufts Chemistry Department. They will shape program strategy, curriculum, admissions, student progress and advising, professional development, program visibility, and recruitment. They will cultivate and sustain relationships with pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, and other external partners and develop and coordinate external work experiences. They will also contribute coursework that complements the Department’s upper\-level and graduate curriculum and draws upon the candidate’s expertise, which may include modern research methods, professional skills, data analysis and interpretation, scientific communication, and chemical entrepreneurship. The successful candidate will be expected to identify opportunities for programmatic growth and innovation across all of these responsibilities.


  
Candidates must hold a PhD in chemistry or a closely related field and have substantial professional experience relevant to the chemical sciences. Candidates should demonstrate a strong commitment to graduate education, mentorship, and professional development. Prior teaching or mentoring experience is preferred and may include undergraduate or graduate teaching, professional education or training, mentorship of trainees or employees, or similar activities. Competitive candidates will have a clear record of leadership and accomplishment in industry, academia, government, or other professional settings, with a demonstrated ability to lead programs, initiatives, teams, or partnerships involving multiple stakeholders. Candidates should demonstrate the ability to develop and implement programmatic initiatives, build consensus, and collaborate effectively across academic and professional communities.


Because external engagement is a central component of this position, the successful candidate should have a strong professional network in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, or related sectors and a demonstrated ability to establish and sustain productive partnerships across academic and professional communities. Experience developing internships, collaborative research or training programs, industry partnerships, or other experiential learning opportunities is particularly desirable. As a Professor of the Practice, the successful candidate will be required to maintain an active professional practice outside of Tufts throughout their appointment.


  
Applicants should submit to https://apply.interfolio.com/ 192860 the following: a cover letter, curriculum vitae, and separate statements of (a) research and/or practice interests, (b) experience in biotechnology/biopharma or other non\-academic settings, and (c) teaching/mentoring experience and philosophy. Applicants of strongest interest will subsequently be contacted to submit three letters of recommendation uploaded directly by recommenders to Interfolio. Review of applications will begin on October 1 and continue until the position is filled.


For questions on this position, please contact Chemistry Department Manager, Joe Hebert at joe.hebert@tufts.edu.

**Description**:


The Department of Chemistry at the University of Houston (UH) invites applications for a tenure\-track/tenured faculty position in synthetic organic chemistry at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor rank. While candidates from all areas of organic chemistry will be considered, we are particularly interested in applicants who will establish an innovative, internationally recognized research program that addresses critical challenges in drug discovery and human health through the application of modern synthetic chemistry.
  

  

Areas of research interest include, but are not limited to, the development of new synthetic methodologies, the design and synthesis of novel therapeutics, and investigations of drug interactions and disease mechanisms. Candidates whose research complements existing strengths at UH and across Texas, particularly in cancer and dementia, are especially encouraged to apply.
  

  

The successful candidate will establish an externally funded experimental research program, teach undergraduate and graduate chemistry courses, mentor students and researchers, and contribute to university service. This appointment is in Chemistry but is intended to support interdisciplinary research that leverages expertise and resources across multiple departments and colleges at the University of Houston. New faculty hires will have opportunities to collaborate with investigators affiliated with the UH Drug Discovery Institute, College of Pharmacy, the Multidisciplinary Institute for Neuroscience and Dementia, and other research centers.
  

  

Applicants must have a PhD in Chemistry and postdoctoral or equivalent industrial or national\-laboratory research experience is preferred. Candidates should demonstrate strong research accomplishments and the potential to perform independent, high\-impact research.
  

  

**Application Instructions**
  

Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, and a one\-page statement of teaching philosophy.
  

  

Candidates applying for appointment at the Assistant Professor level should arrange for three confidential letters of recommendation to be submitted and provide a research statement of no more than five pages describing their future research plans.
  

  

Candidates applying for appointment at the Associate or Full Professor level should submit a one\-page summary of their current research program, highlighting major accomplishments, ongoing activities, and current funding support.
  

  

Review of applications will begin on 10/9/2026 and will continue until the position is filled.  

  

  



Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of Texas for the duration of their appointments.
  

  

Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
  

  

All positions at the University of Houston\-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e., communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems, electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the security and integrity of the research is maintained.
  

  

The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

As a comprehensive institution of the University System of Georgia, Valdosta State University (VSU) is a welcoming, aware, and vibrant community founded on and dedicated to serving our communities' rich and diverse heritages. Through excellence in teaching, basic and applied research, and service, VSU provides rigorous programs and opportunities that enrich our students, our university, and our region. The Department of Mechanical Engineering and Engineering Science (MEES) is the largest department within the William States Lee College of Engineering, staffed by 54 full\-time faculty members and 16 staff members who serve about 2,000 undergraduate and graduate students. There are six active NSF CAREER awardees, and several faculty are recognized as Fellows of leading professional societies. The MEES department is internationally recognized for research programs in advanced manufacturing, precision metrology, battery research, motorsports/automotive engineering, control systems, computational mechanics, as well as emerging areas of research focus such as hypersonics and autonomous vehicles. The Department is home to the Center for Precision Metrology, the Center for Additive Manufacturing of Advanced Ceramics and the Battery Complexity, Autonomous Vehicle and Electrification Research Center. The Department has also recently launched a popular undergraduate concentration in Aerospace Engineering. The College of Engineering is home to the newly established NSF Grid Modernization Engine in the Carolinas and is leading initiatives in several areas of strategic research focus for the university, including Advanced Manufacturing and Metrology, Transformational Energy, and Transportation and Advanced Mobility.
  

**Vacancy Open to** All Candidates
  

**Description of Work**
The University of North Carolina at Charlotte recognizes the differentiation of mission, goals, and objectives inherent in the diversity of disciplines represented by its colleges and departments. Thus, the Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure Track Faculty should be interpreted in the context of the related departmental and collegiate goals.
  

Teaching, Advising, Curriculum and Instructional Development – Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to teaching may include but are not limited to: subject matter competence, course design, course presentation, advising and consultation, directing student research, curriculum and instructional development, and grading student work.
  

Scholarly Research, Creative, and Other Professional Activities – All tenured and tenure\-track faculty are expected to participate in expanding the knowledge base of their academic field by conducting research or engaging in other creative activities as appropriate to the faculty member’s discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to research may include but are not limited to: research/creative activity that generates new knowledge and/or synthesizes and/or integrates existing knowledge, publication, an on\-going agenda for research, scholarly, and creative activity, and are expected to seek extramural support for their work.
  

Service to University, the Public, and the Profession – All tenured and tenure\-track faculty are expected to engage in a program of service appropriate to their discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to service may include but are not limited to: service to the administration and governance of the University, public service, and service to the profession.
  

  

This position is subject to research\-security screening. As part of the application, applicants must disclose, **either in their CV or in a separate document submitted with the application**, all current appointments or affiliations with foreign institutions or organizations, foreign research support, and ongoing research collaborations with foreign institutions, organizations, or their personnel. Before candidates advance to an on\-campus interview, the university will review this information and other publicly available information for relationships involving institutions on the current Section 1286 list and any other applicable U.S. restricted\-party lists. A disclosed or identified relationship does not automatically disqualify a candidate. As a condition of employment, a selected candidate must resolve any relationship the university determines would violate applicable law or sponsor requirements or materially impair the candidate’s or the university’s eligibility for federal funding.
  

  

To view the complete Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure\-Track Faculty document visit our website: https://facultyhandbooks.charlotte.edu/full\-time\-faculty\-handbook/
  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
The Department of Mechanical Engineering and Engineering Science at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte is currently seeking exceptionally qualified candidates for a 9\-month tenure\-track Assistant Professor position with research expertise in solid mechanics and mechanics of materials, and an expected start date of August 2027\. Specific areas of interest include, but are not limited to:  

  

  

* Mechanics of materials in extreme environments
* Nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics mechanics
* Mechanics of advanced composites, architected and multifunctional materials, and adaptive structures

Structural integrity, reliability, and predictive lifetime modeling.  
* 

Candidates working at the intersection of mechanics and emerging technologies are particularly encouraged to apply, including those developing scientific machine learning, quantum computing algorithms, advanced numerical methods, and full\-field or in\-situ experimental techniques. Relevant applications may include aerospace and hypersonic structures, energy systems, materials for nuclear and fusion technologies, and materials and structures subjected to extreme loading or environmental conditions.  

  

  

**Minimum Experience/Education**
UNC Charlotte gives primary consideration to the earned doctorate or terminal degree in the teaching discipline or a related discipline.
  

**Preferred Education, Skills and Experience**
Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in one of the following areas: Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related field by the time of appointment. Applicants should be committed to teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
  

  

It is expected that the successful candidate will build strong collaborations with industry partners and national laboratories, publish in leading research journals, and establish a strong externally funded research program. Applicants should also be committed to supervising undergraduate capstone projects and graduate theses and dissertations. Priority will be given to candidates with strong research records, as evidenced by peer\-reviewed publications, externally funded research, and a plan for future research that aligns with the university’s and department’s research focus in this area.

**Job Description**

The Department of Physics and Astronomy at Montclair State University invites applications for a full\-time, tenure\-track Assistant Professor of Engineering position to begin August 2027\. This position will contribute to the launch of a new Engineering concentration and support the development of the corresponding curriculum.  



  

The ideal applicant will have strong familiarity and experience with the standard curricula for physics and at least one core engineering discipline (especially Mechanical, Aerospace, Electrical, Optical, or Nuclear Engineering). Other engineering or physics disciplines may also be considered. The applicant’s research area should likewise connect with an engineering discipline or a related area of physics or applied physics.  



  

The successful candidate is expected to develop a robust, self\-directed research agenda capable of attracting external funding (startup funding will be available). They will be able to teach a combination of introductory physics courses, advanced laboratory courses, and specialized upper\-level engineering and physics electives. The new faculty will actively mentor undergraduate physics majors, provide advising for career paths in engineering and physics, and offer research opportunities that help students prepare for graduate programs and industry jobs. They will also contribute to departmental growth, curriculum design, and other department service commitments.  



  

The standard annual load for tenure\-track faculty is 12 teaching credit hours (TCH) per semester. The University supports research excellence through the Faculty Scholarship Program (FSP), which provides research\-active faculty with up to 6 TCH of reassigned time per academic year to pursue their scholarly agenda.  



  

**THE DEPARTMENT OF PHYSICS AND ASTRONOMY**

The Department of Physics and Astronomy at Montclair State University was formed in 2018 and consists of 7 faculty members and well over 100 physics majors. Our students represent a diverse population and include many first\-generation college students. In addition to a major and minor in Physics, we also offer a concentration in astronomy and several dual\-degree options, including a 3\+2 BS Physics \+ Master’s in Mechanical Engineering with Stevens Institute of Technology. Additional 3\+2 dual\-degree options involving physics and engineering, as well as an engineering concentration, are under active consideration. Multiple teacher certification pathways are also available. Along with a commitment to effective teaching, research excellence and student involvement in research are key components of our department’s culture. Our faculty are active and internationally recognized in the disciplines of gravitational\-wave physics, astrophysics, optics, and nuclear physics. Current facilities include two introductory teaching labs, a dedicated lab for upper\-level physics courses, a machining/fabrication shop, and dedicated research labs focusing on optics and low\-energy nuclear physics. Other lab facilities available on campus include NMR, AFM, TEM, and ICP\-MS. A new interdisciplinary science building (expected to open in 2028\) will further expand our teaching and research spaces. The department strives to create an atmosphere of collegiality, inclusion, and the promotion of excellence. Additional information about our Department can be found online at https://inside.montclair.edu/colleges\-schools\-research/math\-science/physics\-and\-astronomy\-department  



  

**THE COLLEGE OF SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICS**

The College of Science and Mathematics at Montclair State University empowers the next generation of STEM leaders through rigorous academics, hands\-on discovery, and inclusive excellence. Our mission is grounded in a student\-centered philosophy that values the dedication of our faculty, the curiosity of our students, and a shared commitment to advancing scientific knowledge and innovation. With modern facilities and cutting\-edge technology, we offer distinctive undergraduate and graduate programs across the Departments of Biology, Chemistry and Biochemistry, Earth and Environmental Studies, Mathematics, and Physics and Astronomy and the School of Computing. Through a research\-driven curriculum, community\-engaged learning, and real\-world problem\-solving experiences, CSAM equips students with durable skill sets to meet the demands of an evolving world. By cultivating strong partnerships with industry, government, and nonprofit organizations, the College drives economic growth, advances environmental sustainability, and strengthens the STEM workforce across New Jersey and beyond.  



  

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**REQUIRED:**

* A PhD in Engineering (Mechanical, Aerospace, Electrical, Optical, Nuclear), Physics, Applied Physics, or closely related fields.
* A proven track record of peer\-reviewed publications and a competitive research agenda with clear potential for external funding and that can substantially involve undergraduate students.
* Demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching physics and engineering courses, which readily translates to the Montclair State student body.
Demonstrated interest and commitment to service.  
* 

  

**PREFERRED:**

Prior experience in teaching, working in industry, or postdoctoral research.  

* 

  

**STARTING DATE:** August 27, 2027  



**REQUIRED MATERIALS:**

* Cover letter that briefly summarizes your qualifications, explains your interest in joining our department, and discusses your vision for contributing to an engineering concentration at Montclair.
* Complete curriculum vitae.
* Research Statement (3 to 5 pages) highlighting your research accomplishments, current field of interest, planned future directions or aspirations, potential sources of external funding, and plans for involving undergraduate students.
* Teaching statement (2 to 4 pages) that addresses: (i) your overall approach to teaching; (ii) successful pedagogical strategies for a student population with diverse backgrounds and levels of preparation; and (iii) courses that you envision teaching at Montclair.
Contact information for three to five references, including name, title, affiliation, email, and phone. The search committee will solicit references directly following an initial screening of applicants.  
* 

  

**APPLY BY:**

Applications should be submitted by **December 1, 2026** to ensure full consideration. Initial screening will begin shortly thereafter and be complete by the end of December. On\-campus interviews are expected to take place in February 2027\. The position is open until filled. Questions about this position can be directed to physics\-search@montclair.edu .

**Assistant Professor, Department of Geography**  

  

**Rank:** Assistant Professor  

**Tenure Information:** Tenure Track  

  

**Department Summary:**  

The Department of Geography at Bridgewater State University is accepting applications for a full\-time, tenure track Assistant Professor. Our department is committed to excellence in undergraduate teaching, research, applied geography and outreach. The department offers: B.S. in Geography with concentrations in Environmental Planning and Conservation, and Environmental Sustainability and Climate Resilience; B.A. in Geography with concentrations in Geography for Educators, and Sustainable Global Systems; minors in Geography, Geospatial Science, Urban Studies and Planning; and a post\-graduate certificate in Geographic Information Systems. Our department consists of six full\-time faculty, four part\-time faculty and an administrative assistant, and has dedicated physical/human/geospatial classrooms and laboratories in the Dana Mohler\-Faria Center for Science and Mathematics. Our department serves a diverse student body, with 27% of our students identifying as students of color, and we are committed to further strengthening diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging across our programs and community.  

  

*Bridgewater State University is an inclusive community dedicated to the lifelong success of all students; focused on the continuous improvement of its people; and is responsible for leading innovation that benefits Southeastern Massachusetts, the commonwealth, and the world. Bridgewater's accessible environment of teaching and learning stimulates critical thinking and the pursuit of new knowledge and deeper understanding. The teaching and learning environment at Bridgewater also cultivates meaningful and diverse interpersonal relationships and fosters an appreciation for global engagement aimed at transforming lives and improving the human condition. Our commitment is reflected in our* ***institutional values****, which ensure that all students are supported and succeed.*  


  

**Essential Duties:**  

The Department of Geography at Bridgewater State University is accepting applications for **a full\-time, tenure track Assistant Professor** faculty position, beginning in the Fall of 2027\.  

  

The successful candidate will be a highly motivated individual with expertise in physical geography. Teaching responsibilities include courses in physical geography and geospatial science. The successful candidate is expected to bring new ideas for course offerings related to that candidate's area of expertise that support the department's leadership role in applying geospatial data to problems in sustainability and resilience. A commitment to teaching excellence that supports a diverse student body is essential. This faculty member will help support the geography department's growing undergraduate programs, a new graduate GIS certificate program, collaborations with other BSU programs, and high\-impact practices such as fieldwork, undergraduate research, internships, and service\-learning opportunities.  

  

Essential faculty duties also include participation in departmental meetings, committee work, departmental curriculum development, and advising students in course selection and major progress.  

  

Applicants should be strongly committed to excellence in teaching and service, as well as demonstrate sensitivity to and understanding of students from diverse backgrounds with a wide range of abilities.  


  

**Required Qualifications:**  

A PhD in Geography or a related field. ABD candidates will be considered provided that they will have their PhD in hand by September 1, 2027\.  

  

Experience teaching undergraduate and/or graduate courses.  

  

Demonstrate the ability to teach lecture and laboratory sections.  

  

Demonstrate a well\-developed research plan incorporating undergraduate students into a research program.  

  

Applicants must also demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in teaching, advising, and undergraduate research mentoring that enhances an environment of equity, diversity and inclusion.  

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**  

Teaching and technology expertise.  

  

Expertise in physical geography, geospatial science and undergraduate high impact practices.  

  

**Special Conditions for Eligibility:**  

Please be aware that employment at Bridgewater State University is contingent upon completion of a successful background check. Bridgewater State University is an E\-Verify employer.  

  

Salary is commensurate with experience in accordance with the Appendix O of the **MSCA** **contract**. A reasonable starting salary range to expect for a new faculty member appointed at the rank of Assistant Professor is $75,000 to $85,000\.

**Open Date:** 09/28/2026  

**Close Date:** 12/31/2026  

**Open Until Filled:** No

* A minimum of three (3\) professional reference entries in space provided on the application form.

  

* Resume/CV

  

* Cover Letter

The statement should discuss instructional methods, student engagement, assessment of learning outcomes, and commitment to creating an inclusive, supportive, and effective learning environment for diverse student populations.

The Department of Secondary Education and Educational Leadership (SEEL) invites applications for a full\-time tenure\-track position. The mission of the department is to prepare educators and related professionals to teach, lead, and serve in a diverse and evolving global society. This position requires contractual scheduled office hours for student advising and consultation. Additional responsibilities may include mentoring graduate students and other related duties as assigned and/or required.  

  

The successful candidate will display effective practices for diverse graduate and undergraduate students.  

  

**Required Qualifications:**  

* Ph.D. or Ed.D. in Educational Leadership/School Administration —Candidates who have not yet earned their doctoral degree may be considered, but evidence of an impending successful degree conferral by September 1, 2027 will be required.

* Ability to teach courses on educational leadership, organizational change, education finance, or education law for students who are both K\-12 and higher education professionals in synchronous, asynchronous, hybrid, and face\-to\-face modalities.

  

* Five or more years of experience in PK\-12/16 school administration.

  

* Demonstrated ability to design and teach online graduate and undergraduate courses utilizing effective online/hybrid teaching strategies to promote student learning.

  

* A record of excellence in teaching, service, and or scholarship that demonstrates a commitment to a multicultural work environment that celebrates multiple perspectives.

  


  

**Preferred Qualifications:**  

* Experience and commitment to advising, recruiting, and/or mentoring graduate students.

  

* Evidence of qualitative, quantitative, or mixed\-methods research.

  

* Experience in program assessment, state, and national accreditation standards.

  

* Commitment to excellence in teaching and advising, and to professional work in a multicultural environment that embraces excellence, diversity, and multiple perspectives.

  

* Experience with State, National, and Professional accreditation Standards. MA standards preferred.

  

* Record of professional activities commensurate with the rank of assistant professor.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
jobs.description:
The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln invites applications for a tenure\-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date in the 2027–2028 academic year.  

  

  

The department seeks an outstanding candidate who will establish a nationally visible, externally funded research program in catalysis and contribute to excellence in undergraduate and graduate education. Catalysis is a core discipline in chemical engineering and a central enabling technology for advances in energy, sustainability, advanced materials, agriculture, and value\-added chemical manufacturing.  

  

  

Research areas of interest include, but are not limited to, heterogeneous and homogeneous catalysis; electrocatalysis and photocatalysis; biocatalysis; catalytic materials and interfaces; reaction engineering and kinetics; computational and data\-enabled catalysis; integrated experimental–computational approaches; decarbonization; hydrogen technologies; carbon capture, utilization, and conversion; biofuels and biobased manufacturing; and catalysis for advanced manufacturing. Candidates whose work complements and expands existing departmental strengths are encouraged to apply.  

  

  

The successful candidate will be expected to develop a strong scholarly record and externally funded research program; teach undergraduate and graduate courses in chemical engineering, including courses related to reaction engineering, kinetics, and catalysis as appropriate; mentor undergraduate and graduate students; and contribute to departmental, college, and university service. The position offers opportunities for collaboration with faculty engaged in experimental and computational catalysis and with campus research entities including the Nebraska Center for Materials and Nanoscience and the Nebraska Energy Sciences Research Center.  

  

  

The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering provides an outstanding environment for research and education, with opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration across the University of Nebraska–Lincoln and the broader University of Nebraska system. The department’s strategic growth in catalysis will support research and workforce development in areas important to Nebraska and the broader Midwest while enhancing competitiveness for federal and collaborative research initiatives.
Minimum Required Qualifications
* A Ph.D. or equivalent terminal degree by the time of appointment. At least one degree (B.S., M.S., and/or Ph.D.) must be in chemical engineering.
* A record of strong scholarly achievement.
* A demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate and graduate education.
* The potential to establish a strong externally\-funded research program.

Preferred Qualifications
* Research areas of interest include, but are not limited to, heterogeneous and homogeneous catalysis; electrocatalysis and photocatalysis; biocatalysis; catalytic materials and interfaces; reaction engineering and kinetics; computational and data\-enabled catalysis; integrated experimental–computational approaches; decarbonization; hydrogen technologies; carbon capture, utilization, and conversion; biofuels and biobased manufacturing; and catalysis for advanced manufacturing.

  
Posted Salary
  
How to Apply
Click “Apply for this Job,” complete the faculty information form, and attach the following documents:
* Cover letter explaining the applicant’s interest in the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

* A combined research and teaching statement (four pages total, with a minimum of one page devoted to teaching).

* Names and contact information for three professional references.


Please combine the statements (items 3, 4, and 5\) into a single document and attach as “Other Document.” For more information about the position, please contact Rajib Saha, rsaha2@nebraska.edu.

The Department of Biomedical Engineering in the Cullen College of Engineering at the University of Houston is seeking a tenure\-track Assistant Professor or tenured Associate Professor of Biomedical Engineering. This highly multidisciplinary position is intended to expand the University of Houston’s strengths in imaging, biomaterials, tissue engineering, regenerative engineering, and translational biomedical engineering.
  

  

The ideal candidate will develop an independent research program focused on the design, fabrication, characterization, imaging, and biological evaluation of advanced biomaterials for tissue repair, regeneration, and disease modeling. The ideal candidate should have notable experience with imaging, 3D\-printed and advanced\-manufactured biomaterial platforms, including extracellular matrix\-derived, decellularized, mineralized collagen, cryogel, polymer\-ceramic, and/or composite scaffold systems. Areas of interest include musculoskeletal tissue engineering; bone, cartilage, and osteochondral repair; osteoarthritis modeling and treatment; drug delivery; and biomaterial strategies that modulate inflammation, macrophage polarization, mesenchymal stem cell behavior, osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and other cell\-material interactions. Experience with high\-throughput scaffold or biomaterial screening platforms, in vitro co\-culture systems, quantitative materials characterization, microscopy\-based analysis such as multiphoton microscopy, and relevant preclinical models is highly desirable.
  

  

The successful candidate should demonstrate the ability to connect imaging and biomaterials innovation with clinically relevant questions, including the development of translational approaches for improved tissue repair, implanted material response, and regenerative medicine. The candidate should be prepared to build collaborations with faculty across engineering, medicine, cancer biology, orthopedics, materials science, and translational research, and to contribute to interdisciplinary institutes and externally funded team science.
  

  

The candidate should have a strong publication record, a record of technical presentations, experience preparing competitive funding applications, and a clear plan for building an externally funded research program. The candidate should also have strong teaching and mentoring experience and be prepared to teach undergraduate and graduate courses in biomedical engineering, biomaterials, tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and related quantitative engineering topics.
