Anticipated start: July 1, 2027 Application Window
  
**Open date:** September 25, 2026
  
**Next review date:** Monday, Nov 9, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.
  
**Final date:** Monday, Nov 9, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Applications will continue to be accepted until this date. Position description
  
The Department of Electrical Engineering \& Computer Sciences (EECS) and the Center for Computational Biology (CCB) at UC Berkeley invite applications for one approved tenure\-track position at the Assistant Professor level in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) for biology. Memberships in related institutes and initiatives or affiliations with other UC Berkeley departments or schools may also be considered. The EECS Department and the Center for Computational Biology have several related faculty positions open or opening soon. Please visit our EECS Faculty Positions website and the CCB Careers website to view these listings. If you are qualified for and wish to be considered for more than one position, please submit a separate application for each.
  
**About the Department :** The EECS department is part of the College of Engineering (COE) and the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It offers one of the strongest research and instructional programs in this field anywhere in the world. The department's key strength is its array of cross\-disciplinary, team\-driven projects. The integration of EE and CS forms the core, with strong interactions that extend into many other disciplines.
  
**About the Center :** CCB is an academic unit under the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It offers a PhD degree program, as well as interdisciplinary collaboration and research for diverse areas across computational biology. The center features distinguished faculty and graduate students from more than a dozen academic departments across six colleges at UC Berkeley.
  
**About the Position :** EECS and CCB are seeking applicants developing innovative AI and machine learning (ML) methods that significantly advance our understanding of complex biological systems and address high\-impact problems in biology. Relevant research areas include, but are not limited to the following: AI/ML for predicting cellular phenotypes and responses to genetic, molecular, and environmental perturbations; modeling of molecular interactions, including interactions among proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules; genotype\-to\-phenotype prediction across molecular, cellular, and organismal scales; AI/ML for genome and biomolecule engineering; and method development for computational genomics, including the integration of large\-scale single\-cell, spatial, imaging, and multimodal biological data. Across these areas, we are particularly interested in candidates who develop novel and broadly applicable AI/ML methodology for learning from complex biological data, with the potential to uncover fundamental biological principles and enable new approaches to understanding, predicting, and manipulating biological systems.
  
UC Berkeley values the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples, single parents, or those who may have taken time off for family reasons. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit the Office for Faculty Equity and Welfare's website . Qualifications Basic qualifications (required at time of application)
  
Completion of a doctoral degree (e.g., PhD), or equivalent international degree, or enrolled in a doctoral degree or equivalent international degree\-granting program at the time of application. Preferred qualifications
  
Preference will be given to applicants interested in AI and machine learning methods development that advance the understanding of complex biological systems as well as to applicants whose research, teaching, or service has prepared them to contribute to our commitment to create, educate, and serve our society. Application Requirements Document requirements
  
  

Cover Letter
  
  

Curriculum Vitae \- Your most recently updated C.V. with complete list of publications. Please list prior academic, professional and/or public service activities and future service interests. This can include, for example, participating in professional or scientific associations, serving on committees that advance department, campus or discipline goals, and conducting outreach activities that can remove barriers and increase participation of academics in your field.
  
  

Statement of Research \- Please discuss prior research accomplishments and future plans. This can include, for example, your publication record, awards, presentations, inclusive research practices, communication skills, and collaborations that promote the excellence of your research, and areas for future research. Maximum of five pages, excluding references.
  
  

Statement of Teaching and Mentoring \- Please discuss prior teaching experience, teaching approach, and future teaching interests. This can include, for example, specific efforts and accomplishments, and future plans to support the success of all students through inclusive curriculum, classroom environment, and pedagogy. Please also discuss your mentoring experiences and approach. This can include, for example, past efforts and future plans to support the success of all students, and to foster an inclusive research mentoring environment that removes barriers and promotes equitable access and advancement of the research program. You might include a list of UC Berkeley courses you would feel comfortable teaching.
  
  

Significant Publication 1 \- Please provide a statement that summarizes the significance of the selected publication and include the PDF hyperlink.
  
  

Significant Publication 2 \- Please provide a statement that summarizes the significance of the selected publication and include the PDF hyperlink.
  
  

Significant Publication 3 \- Please provide a statement that summarizes the significance of the selected publication and include the PDF hyperlink.
  
  

Authorization to Release Information Form \- An institutional reference check will be completed only if you are selected as the candidate to whom the hiring unit would like to extend a formal offer. Download, complete, sign, and upload the Authorization to Release Information form . Reference requirements
  
3 letters of reference required
  
Applicants must provide three letters of recommendation that speak to their record and/or potential for excellence in research, teaching, mentoring, and service. Recommenders providing letters of reference should submit them as early as possible, preferably by the application deadline. Applicants are responsible for asking their references to upload letters as part of the online application process. Apply link: https://aprecruit.berkeley.edu/JPF05560
  
**Help contact:** monica.aiello@berkeley.edu About UC Berkeley
  
UC Berkeley is committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging in our public mission of research, teaching, and service, consistent with UC Regents Policy 4400 and University of California Academic Personnel policy ( APM 210 1\-d ). These values are embedded in our Principles of Community , which reflect our passion for critical inquiry, debate, discovery and innovation, and our deep commitment to contributing to a better world. Every member of the UC Berkeley community has a role in sustaining a safe, caring and humane environment in which these values can thrive.
  
The University of California, Berkeley is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, or protected veteran status.
  
For more information, please refer to the University of California's Affirmative Action and Nondiscrimination in Employment Policy and the University of California's Anti\-Discrimination Policy .
  
In searches when letters of reference are required all letters will be treated as confidential per University of California policy and California state law. Please refer potential referees, including when letters are provided via a third party (i.e., dossier service or career center), to the UC Berkeley statement of confidentiality prior to submitting their letter.
  
As a University employee, you will be required to comply with all applicable University policies and/or collective bargaining agreements, as may be amended from time to time. Federal, state, or local government directives may impose additional requirements.
  
The University of California is committed to creating and maintaining a community dedicated to the advancement, application, and transmission of knowledge and creative endeavors through academic excellence, where all individuals who participate in University programs and activities can work and learn together in a safe and secure environment, free of violence, harassment, or discrimination. Consistent with this commitment, UC Berkeley requires all applicants for Senate faculty positions to complete, sign, and upload an Authorization of Information Release form into AP Recruit as part of their application. If an applicant does not include the signed authorization, the application will be considered incomplete, and as with any incomplete application, will not receive further consideration. Although all applicants for faculty recruitments must complete the entire application, applicants will only be subject to institutional reference checks if and when they are selected as the candidate to whom the hiring unit would like to extend a formal offer. More information is available on this website .
  
As a condition of employment, the finalist will be required to disclose if they are subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct.
  
“Misconduct” means any violation of the policies or laws governing conduct at the applicant's previous place of employment, including, but not limited to, violations of policies or laws prohibiting sexual harassment, sexual assault, or other forms of harassment or discrimination, as defined by the employer.

**Job Summary**
---------------


The Phillip M. Drayer Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Lamar University invites applications for a tenure\-track Assistant Professor position in Computer Engineering, beginning Fall 2026\. Candidates with strong records of funded research and industrial experience may be considered for appointment at the Associate Professor level..


We seek candidates who will develop a vigorous, externally funded research program and excel in teaching at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. While strong applicants in all areas of computer engineering will be considered, special consideration will be given to candidates with research or industrial experience in semiconductors, microchip design, and advanced embedded systems, including but not limited to:


* Device fabrication, semiconductor materials, and nanostructures.
* Microprocessor and microcontroller design.
* Integrated circuit layout, verification, and testing.
* Hardware security for microchips and embedded systems.
* Digital and mixed\-signal IC design.
* Emerging semiconductor technologies (neuromorphic, photonic, RF, wide\-bandgap, etc.).
* Embedded systems, real\-time systems, and edge computing hardware.
* VLSI design, ASIC design, and SoC/NoC architectures.

The successful candidate will:


* Teach core and elective courses in computer engineering at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
* Supervise student projects, theses, and dissertations.
* Establish and maintain an impactful research program.
* Collaborate with industry and government partners.
* Contribute to departmental, college, and university service.

The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching, research, and service missions of the department.


**Teaching:**
  

Develop and deliver undergraduate and graduate courses in electrical engineering, in alignment with the department’s curriculum and educational goals. Provide effective instruction, academic advising, and mentorship to students. Utilize innovative teaching practices to promote student engagement and learning.


**Research:**
  

Establish and maintain an independent, externally funded research program in an area relevant to electrical engineering. Conduct impactful research, publish in peer\-reviewed journals, and present findings at national and international conferences. Engage in interdisciplinary collaborations and pursue partnerships with industry, government agencies, and academic institutions.


**Service:**
  

Contribute to the department, college, and university through committee work, curriculum development, and participation in accreditation efforts. Support outreach and recruitment initiatives and represent the department at professional events and in community engagement activities. Participate in academic governance and contribute to the advancement of the discipline.


**Essential Job Functions**
---------------------------


* Develop and deliver undergraduate and graduate courses in chemical or biomolecular engineering, aligned with the department’s curriculum and learning objectives. Provide effective instruction, mentorship, and academic advising to students. Employ innovative teaching methods and technologies to enhance student learning outcomes.
* Establish and lead an independent, externally funded research program in an area of chemical or biomolecular engineering. Conduct high\-impact research, publish scholarly articles in peer\-reviewed journals, and present findings at national and international conferences. Collaborate with interdisciplinary research teams and pursue partnerships with industry and government agencies.
* Contribute to departmental, university, and professional activities, including committee assignments, curriculum development, accreditation processes, and outreach initiatives. Participate in academic governance, engage in community service, and represent the department at professional conferences and events.
**Minimum and Desired Qualifications**
--------------------------------------


**Minimum Qualifications:**
* Undergraduate and Ph.D. degrees from an accredited university in computer engineering or a closely related field. (The Ph.D. must be completed by Aug. 2027\.)
* Bachelor’s and Ph.D. degrees in Computer Engineering. The Ph.D. must be completed by August 2027\. Degrees in Electrical Engineering can be accepted if the applicant has research and/or industrial experience in Computer Engineering related areas.
* Demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching and research.
* Evidence of the ability to attract external funding.
* Strong communication skills.

**Desired Qualifications:*** Experience teaching electrical and computer engineering courses.
* Experience writing competitive research proposals and securing external funding.
* Relevant industrial experience or postdoctoral research experience.
**Supplemental Information**
----------------------------


**Key Competencies:**
* Demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching, research, and scholarly activity.
* Ability to direct master and doctoral theses.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in a collaborative academic environment.
* Evidence of research productivity, including peer\-reviewed publications and successful grant proposals.
* Experience or interest in utilizing innovative teaching methods and technologies to enhance student learning outcomes.
* Ability to contribute to the department’s mission and strategic goals through teaching excellence, research productivity, and service to the profession.

**Physical Requirements:**
* Able to lift 25 lbs and be able to perform a variety of physical tasks including lifting, bending, stooping, squatting, stair climbing and walking between buildings.

**Job Conditions:**
* Position requires on\-campus teaching, research, and service activities.
* Occasional evening and weekend work and travel may be required to support university business, research activities, professional development, and conferences.

  

**Special Note:**
* We are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position.
* Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

**Who We Are:**
* Home to more than 18,000 students, Lamar University is among the fastest growing Texas colleges and universities. LU is a member of The Texas State University System, which is the first higher education system of Texas and maintains the lowest average tuition and fees of any university system in Texas. With more than 120\-degree options and a community that cares, Lamar students are always proud to be Cardinals. Lamar University strives to educate leaders, demonstrate excellence in student learning and career readiness, and pursue research with relevance.
* Lamar University is committed to fostering an environment of teamwork where all students, faculty, and staff can learn, work, and become a part of our community.

**Benefits:**
* Health, dental \& vision insurance.
* Life insurance.
* State of Texas Retirement plans.
* Tuition covered at 100% for employees, spouses and/or eligible dependents.
* Paid time off – vacation, sick, and holidays.

To see more information about the available benefits, please visit: Benefits \- Lamar University  

  

*Lamar University is An Equal Opportunity Employer*


*Lamar University is proud to provide employment preference to veteran applicants in accordance with Texas 805 Government Code, Section 657\.003\.*


*This position is security\-sensitive and thereby subject to the provisions of the Texas Education Code §51\.215, which authorizes the employer to obtain criminal history record information.*

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Organic Chemistry
jobs.description:
**Job no:** 541514  

**Work type:** Tenure\-Track Faculty  

**Location:** Main Campus (Gainesville, FL)  

**Categories:** Education/Training/Instructional Design, Grant or Research Administration  

**Department:**16120100 \- LS\-CHEMISTRY\-GENERAL  


**Classification Title:**

Assistant/Associate Professor

  

  

**Classification Minimum Requirements:**

Ph.D. in Chemistry or closely related field.

  

  

**Job Description:**

The University of Florida, Department of Chemistry, invites applications for a full\-time, nine\-month, tenure\-accruing position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor in Organic Chemistry, broadly defined. The appointments will commence on August 16, 2027\.



Successful candidates are expected to conduct innovative research at the highest level and to establish an outstanding, independent, externally funded research program. We seek candidates with a record of excellence in research and scholarship, the ability to excel in teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels and who will contribute to the service mission of the Department of Chemistry and the University of Florida. For more information about the Department of Chemistry, please visit our website, www.chem.ufl.edu.


The University of Florida is a land grant, sea grant, and space grant university and home to the most comprehensive university health sciences facilities in the southeast. UF is located in Gainesville, a city of approximately 150,000 residents in North\-Central Florida, 50 miles from the Gulf, and 67 miles from the Atlantic Ocean, and within a 2\-hour drive to large metropolitan areas (Orlando, Tampa, Jacksonville). The beautiful climate and extensive nearby parks and recreational areas afford year\-round outdoor activities, including hiking, biking, and nature photography. UF’s large college sports programs, museums, and performing arts center support a range of activities and cultural events for residents to enjoy. Alachua County schools are highly rated and offer a variety of programs including magnet schools and an international baccalaureate program. Learn more about what Gainesville has to offer at Visit Gainesville.
  

**Expected Salary:**

The salary is competitive and commensurate with rank, qualifications and experience.



UF offers a strong benefits package for eligible faculty appointments, including health insurance, paid leave (as applicable), and retirement options. Learn more here.

  

  

**Required Qualifications:**

Ph.D. in Chemistry or closely related field.

  

  

**Preferred:** Postdoctoral experience is desirable.
  

**Special Instructions to Applicants:**

For full consideration, applications must be submitted online. Click on at the top of this posting.



A complete application includes:


* Letter of application summarizing the applicant's qualifications, interests, and suitability for the position.
* A complete *curriculum vitae.*
* Names and contact information for three professional references.
* A brief research summary
* A description of proposed research projects.
* A statement of teaching philosophy.


Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and will continue until a successful applicant is selected.



All candidates for employment are subject to a pre\-employment screening which includes a review of criminal records, reference checks, and verification of education.



The selected candidate will be required to provide an official transcript to the hiring department upon hire. A transcript will not be considered “official” if a designation of “Issued to Student” is visible. Degrees earned from an educational institution outside of the United States require evaluation by a professional credentialing service provider approved by the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES), which can be found at http://www.naces.org/.

  

  

**Health Assessment Required:** No  


**Advertised:** 25 Sep 2026 Eastern Daylight Time  

**Applications close:** Open until filled

Position Summary
**Brief Description of PSU/School/Dept**
**Portland State University** is Oregon’s most affordable public research university, located in the heart of one of America’s most dynamic cities. Our mission to “let knowledge serve the city” reflects our dedication to turning ideas into action — in Portland and around the world. The city is our campus, giving students unmatched access to career connections, a vibrant cultural scene and hands\-on learning experiences with hundreds of community partners. We are proud of our world\-class faculty, groundbreaking research and international reputation for excellence in sustainability, community engagement and innovation.
  

  

**PSU’s Department of World Languages and Literatures** plays a central role in preparing students to function in the global community. We offer courses in 17 languages, and our classes are designed to help you develop proficiency in reading, writing, listening, and speaking for eventual use in a broad variety of real\-world settings.
  

  

**Portland State’s Russian Flagship Program** is an innovative undergraduate program that helps students gain professional levels of proficiency in Russian while pursuing any major at PSU. Russian Flagship students come from many majors, including Mathematics, International Studies, Computer Science, Political Science, History, and many others.
  

  

With generous scholarships for study abroad, the program gives students the opportunity to add real international experience to their major. At graduation, they are global professionals who have professional level skills in Russian and a knowledge of your major field. Our graduates have gone on to work in education, non\-governmental organizations, international businesses, and government agencies, including the U.S. State Department and Department of Defense.
  

**Position Summary**
The Program Coordinator supports and promotes the PSU Russian Flagship Program, whose mission is to encourage undergraduate students of any major to develop professional level fluency in Russian. In consultation with the Flagship Program Director, the Program Coordinator manages the Russian Flagship’s daily operations. In collaboration with Flagship Program Director and the Russian faculty, the Program Coordinator recruits and advises students about the program. The schedule will be 40 hours per week, generally 8am\-5pm, with occasional early start to accommodate student needs. This position will travel occasionally to National Flagship Meetings, and for local recruitment.

* BA Degree.
* Two years of experience in working in an administrative capacity.
* Excellent organizational and office skills.
* Basic computer proficiency, experience working with spreadsheets.
* Demonstrated communication and writing skills, including writing for publication online and in social media.
  

**Preferred Qualifications**
* BA in foreign language, linguistics, international area studies.
* Study abroad or international educational experience.
* Experience working in U.S. higher education.
  

**Key Cultural Competencies**
* Create an environment that acknowledges, encourages, and celebrates differences.
* Function and communicate effectively and respectfully within the context of varying beliefs, behaviors, orientations, identities, and cultural backgrounds.
* Seek opportunities to gain experience working and collaborating in diverse, multicultural, and inclusive settings with a willingness to change for continual improvement.
* Adhere to all of PSU’s policies including the policies on Prohibited Discrimination \& Harassment and the Professional Standards of Conduct.
  

**Environmental Stewardship**
Contributes to a culture of environmental stewardship, practices resource conservation, and actively works toward achieving long\-term sustainability goals.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Engineering Technologies and Applied Design 3-Year Continuing Non-Tenurable
jobs.description:
*Please note that references provided at the time of application for staff positions will not be contacted until the applicant has been offered the position.*


**Description:**
----------------


The Engineering Technologies and Applied Design (ETAD) department at Berea College is seeking a dynamic faculty member for an Assistant Professor, Non\-Tenure/Continuing, 3\-Year position starting August 2027\. While the specific area of expertise is open, **candidates in Sustainable Design, Construction, Architecture, and Engineering/ Engineering Technology** **fields are encouraged to apply.**


We are seeking an educator dedicated to a hands\-on and project\-based curriculum. The successful candidate will guide students through the complete design\-prototype\-test\-production cycle from identifying project needs and research solutions to prototyping, testing, and fabricating finished products. Additionally, the candidate may coordinate with our department technician to instruct students in the safe and skilled operation of woodworking and/or metal processing tools using both automated and manual power equipment, including a range of industrial CNC machines.


**Teaching Responsibilities:**


The ideal candidate will teach department core courses, electives, and contribute to Berea College’s general education program. Expected department courses **may** include:


* ETAD 115 Construction Technology
* ETAD 345: Sustainable Building design
* ETAD 140: Production in Woods
Candidate is also encouraged to develop courses specific to their background.


Following long\-standing tradition and practice at Berea College, this position includes responsibility for supervising, mentoring, and developing students in the College's integrated Work College Program. This supports student learning, career readiness, and the program's learning goals and outcomes. The Work College Program provides a developmental framework that guides student learning while creating a structured mentorship opportunity, with role\-specific training that equips faculty and staff mentors to support student development. Faculty and staff mentors play an essential part in helping students connect their work\-learning\-service experiences with broader academic, professional, and personal development. For faculty, this aligns with Berea's tenure and promotion criteria. Our department actively collaborates with external partners to give students hands\-on experience with outside clients. While not required, the successful candidate is strongly encouraged to integrate community partner projects into their courses.


**Qualifications:**


A master’s degree or higher in **Sustainable Design, Construction, Architecture, and Engineering/ Engineering Technology** **fields,** or other closely related fields is required.


Teaching experience and/or industry experience is also appreciated. Most importantly, given the nature of technology, colleagues are expected to participate in the continued development of content, curriculum, and pedagogy. Ideal candidates would embrace this practice through professional development and active participation in the evolving fields.


**Application:**


Candidates should submit a cover letter, a current curriculum vitae, graduate transcripts, a teaching philosophy, design portfolio (if available) and contact information for three references. Review of applications will begin **November 1, 2026**, and continue until the position is filled.


Founded in 1855, Berea College is nationally recognized as the first coeducational and interracial college in the South. Berea has a longstanding commitment to interracial education and is one of the most racially diverse private liberal arts colleges in the United States. With an emphasis on service to Appalachia and beyond, Berea enrolls more than 1,500 students from 44 states and U.S. territories and more than 60 countries. Berea College admits students who are unable to afford tuition and provides every enrolled student with a fully funded degree that covers 100% of tuition, housing, food, supplies, and fees without loans, for all four years. Berea’s students excel in the College’s supportive yet demanding academic environment, and most are the first in their families to attend college. As one of only 10 federally recognized Work Colleges, all Berea students work 10\-12 hours weekly in various positions across campus, building professional skills in a real\-world learning environment. *Washington Monthly* ranked Berea College the \#1 Best College for your Tuition and Tax Dollars, 2025\. Berea also ranks \#1 in educational access by *The New York Times*, 2023 and \#1 for lowest educational debt by *U.S. News and World Report*, 2025 and 2026\. Berea College is also the only institution in Kentucky to receive the 5\-Star Rating from *Money Magazine,* 2026\.


Located where the Bluegrass Region meets the Cumberland Mountains, the town of Berea (pop. 17,000\) lies 40 miles south of Lexington and is approximately two hours from Cincinnati, Louisville, and Knoxville. More information about Berea College is available at www.berea.edu.


*Berea College, in light of its mission in the tradition of impartial love and social equality, welcomes all people of the earth to learn and work here.*


  
**Our Benefits:**
  

Berea College offers a comprehensive benefits package to eligible employees and their families including health care, dental, vision, retirement, health savings accounts, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, short\-term disability, long\-term disability and an Employee Assistance Program. The benefit package also includes access to the Child Development Laboratory for children of College Staff, ages 6 weeks to 6 years, Seabury Center Membership, Staff Development Funds and Tuition Reimbursement.
  

  

Eligible staff employees also receive paid holidays, vacation, and sick leave.
  

  

Part\-time employees who work an average of twenty\-four hours per week over the course of a year, receive benefits on a pro\-rated basis.  

  

  

**Our Unique Culture:**
  

Berea College strives to be a place where people with various Christian interpretations, different religious traditions, and no religious traditions work together in support of Berea's Great Commitments.
  

  

Over the past century, various leaders of the College have applied the College’s inclusive scriptural foundation and spirit to their expanding world and welcomed those whose beliefs were consistent with the Christian gospel of impartial love. Therefore, Berea College today affirms its inclusive Christian tradition even as it respects the traditions of Jews, Muslims, Buddhists, and Hindus, as well as other faiths, and those holding no religious beliefs. We strive not to ignore our differences, but rather seek to understand each other honestly and respectfully, and together create a climate where anyone can openly discuss what they believe without fear of sanction. To that end, all persons who are willing to share in the spirit and the work of the Great Commitments as shaped by its preamble are welcome to study, to teach, and to work at Berea
  

  

**Labor Supervision:**
  

In support of Berea College’s great commitments, staff and faculty serve as labor supervisors. Our fourth great commitment, The Dignity of Labor, promotes learning and serving in community through the student Labor Program, honoring the dignity and utility of all work, mental and manual, and taking pride in work well done. Student Labor Supervision includes scheduling, assigning, and approving student work, developing students' workplace acumen, and providing tangible work experience. To learn more about the labor program office please see the following link Labor Program Office.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of English
jobs.description:
Georgetown College seeks applications for a full\-time tenure\-track Assistant Professor of English, beginning August 2027\. The successful candidate will have either a Ph.D. or MFA and will be qualified to teach fiction writing and American literature. The position carries a 4/4 load per academic year, including composition and literature surveys. Editing experience or experience teaching editing and publishing is desirable, since the successful candidate will have the opportunity to teach in our new Editing and Publishing minor.
  
  

Located in Georgetown, Kentucky, Georgetown College is a private, Christian, liberal arts institution of approximately 1,200 undergraduate students, and emphasis is placed on teaching excellence in a diverse context. However, in keeping with its firm commitment to academic freedom, no creed or statement of faith is imposed upon employees, nor is any one theological orientation or expression of spirituality singled out for special favor.
  
  

Screening will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. To be considered for the position, send letter of application, vita, unofficial transcripts, statement of teaching philosophy, three letters of recommendation, and a fiction writing sample. A critical essay may be included as well.

jobs.description:
**Job Title**


Assistant Professor of Supply Chain Management**Agency**


Texas A\&M University \- Central Texas**Department**


College of Business Administration**Proposed Minimum Salary**


Commensurate**Job Location**


Killeen, Texas**Job Type**


Faculty**Job Description**


The College of Business Administration (COBA) at Texas A\&M University\-Central Texas welcomes highly qualified applicants to fill an immediate need for an Assistant Professor of Supply Chain Management starting in Fall 2027\. This is a tenure\-track faculty position. Application reviews will begin immediately. We are looking for a collegial teacher\-scholar with a passion for teaching and a multi\-faceted track record of excellence both within and beyond the classroom. Our greatest and immediate teaching need is for undergraduate courses in support of our brand\-new BBA in Logistics \& Supply Chain Management program. Our hope is that this faculty member will help establish this as a strong program with great student outcomes and robust regional industry connections. Courses at other levels and in other related areas may also be available on a limited basis depending on applicant qualifications and interest.

 **About Texas A\&M University – Central Texas**


Established as an independent member of the Texas A\&M University System in 2009, A\&M\-Central Texas is a friendly and dynamic regional teaching institution that prides itself on excellence in instruction but also embraces a growing emphasis on research. A\&M\-Central Texas is truly unique in that it is an upper\- and masters\-level institution, offering only junior\- and senior\-level coursework needed to successfully complete baccalaureate degrees and all coursework leading to the completion of master’s degrees. As such, A\&M\-Central Texas maintains active partnerships with the major community colleges within the Greater Austin and Central Texas regions, as well as with Fort Hood, a premier outpost of the U.S. Army and one of the largest military installations in the world. Our multifaceted student demographic includes a significant proportion of first\-generation college students, non\-traditional learners, and military\-affiliated personnel.

  

The College of Business Administration is accredited by AACSB, and we are eager to have energetic and collegial new faculty members partner with us in pursuit of our major strategic initiatives, of which there are many on the near horizon (most notably, a DBA program anticipated to launch Fall 2027 pending SACSCOC final approval). This is an exciting time of rapid change within the University and College that affords new faculty members many opportunities to make an immediate, significant, and lasting impact.

  

A\&M\-Central Texas is located on the southern edge of Killeen, TX, a city of approximately 150,000 located about halfway between Austin and Waco—about 60 miles either way. Our faculty members enjoy a wide variety of living options by virtue of the range of communities in the area—from quiet and rural to bustling and cosmopolitan. It is an easy drive to great art, food, shopping, and night life as well as to hunting, fishing, hiking, and camping for those who prefer the outdoors. Central Texas is a rapidly growing region with a booming economy, but is also a great place for families, with many options for schooling, worship, civic engagement, and recreation. It also has modest traffic and a reasonable cost of living. The major metropolitan areas of Houston, Dallas\-Fort Worth, and San Antonio are all within a 3\-hour radius of Killeen.

 **Responsibilities:**

The candidate will be expected to provide quality, engaging instruction for typically three courses per term, primarily at the undergraduate level and in a variety of course delivery formats (face\-to\-face, online, or hybrid), with fully online being the most in\-demand option at present. Candidates who possess exceptional skill at making technical content accessible to a broad audience are especially desired. The candidate will be expected to teach the following courses: LSCM 4321 Production and Operations Management, LSCM 4322 Business Process, Quality, and Lean Management, LSCM 4326 Global Procurement and Strategic Sourcing. Other assigned courses may include LSCM 4323 Supply Chain Management and BUSI 3311 Business Statistics. Additional summer teaching opportunities may be available depending on student demand and department needs.

  

Some scholarly contributions are also required. The candidate is expected have sufficient scholarly and/or professional activities to have “scholarly academic” status upon arrival per AACSB faculty classifications, and to have a healthy pipeline of works in progress toward publication, where health is measured more by viability and anticipated impact than by number and/or status. Scholarship is but one category of currency and impact with which faculty may engage: others include maintaining a recognized professional certification, presenting at academic conferences, engaging in consulting or other industry\-related activities, and completing other relevant professional training and development activities. Professional development funds are available to support all of these endeavors, and faculty within the College frequently collaborate on research projects together.

  

In regard to service, faculty are expected to support their program(s), department, college, and/or university with committee work, but first\-year faculty are exempt from this. In addition, faculty are expected to have some sort of service to their profession and/or to the community, but again, service contribution impact and quality are more important than the numbers of activities engaged in. Faculty generally have a lot of discretion in determining how best they can add value through their various service activities.

 ***A Presidential Proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on all new H‑1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025, and Texas A\&M University–Central Texas will not pay this fee. Additionally, a moratorium issued by Governor Abbott on January 27, 2026, restricts the filing of new H‑1B petitions unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate. Applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer.***

 **Minimum Qualifications:**


To be eligible to apply for this position, candidates should:

* Possess a terminal degree (doctorate) in supply chain management or a closely related discipline from a regionally accredited university.
* Be eligible for the AACSB “scholarly academic” faculty classification (two publications or relevant terminal degree completed since 2022, with viable works in progress).
* Have a documented track record of successfully teaching supply chain or operations courses, including in fully online formats.
* Be qualified to teach LSCM 4321, LSCM 4322, and LSCM 4326\.

 **Preferred Qualifications:**


The ideal candidate for this position would also possess:

* At least three (3\) years of full\-time collegiate teaching experience.
* Industry experience.
* Experience developing industry connections in support of academic programs.
* Proficiency in creating original and engaging online course instructional materials.
* Qualifications to teach LSCM 4323 and BUSI 3311\.
* Great administrative, organizational, and interpersonal skills to support successful instruction to a largely non\-traditional, first\-generation, and military\-affiliated student body.
* Familiarity/experience with DBA programs and/or supervision of doctoral students.

 **Salary:** Commensurate

**Hours:** Faculty hours; M\-F; hours may vary by assignment and course modality.  



  

**To Apply:**


Please apply directly on our Texas A\&M University\-Central Texas Job Site. Applicants are required to submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae (CV), and either the contact information for three professional references or three letters of recommendation. Additional materials, such as a teaching philosophy statement and transcripts, are optional but strongly encouraged.


All positions are security\-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.


Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

The Department of Accounting and Finance in the Austin E. Cofrin School of Business at the University of Wisconsin\-Green Bay seeks applicants for a tenure\-track position in Finance (Financial Planning) at the Assistant or Associate Professor level.  



  

The Cofrin School of Business is building a distinctive financial planning program that integrates outstanding teaching, applied student learning, scholarship, professional engagement, and community impact. The successful candidate will join a growing program supported by the Charles Schwab Foundation Center for Financial Wellness and Willie D. Davis Finance \& Investment Laboratory, providing exceptional opportunities to connect financial planning education with experiential learning, industry engagement, and community service.  



  

The Cofrin School of Business prioritizes teaching excellence, learner success, quality scholarship, engagement with the regional business community, and meaningful institutional, community, and professional service. Professional experience in financial planning, wealth management, finance, or related areas is viewed favorably. Candidates interested in exploring the intersection of human\-centered financial planning and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, FinTech, and other technologies transforming financial services, are strongly encouraged to apply.  



  

The successful applicant will contribute to a young, growing, forward\-looking School and department embedded within Wisconsin’s third\-largest metropolitan area. Northeast Wisconsin offers significant opportunities for collaboration with the financial services and broader business community, while Green Bay provides an affordable and high\-quality place to live. The Cofrin School of Business and UW–Green Bay continue a sustained record of growth, creating opportunities for faculty interested in helping shape the future of a growing business school and financial planning program.


**Key Job Responsibilities:**
-----------------------------

* Teach a variety of undergraduate and/or graduate courses in financial planning and finance.
* Prepare students for success on the CFP® Certification Examination and careers in financial planning and related financial services fields.
* Develop and support high\-impact experiential learning opportunities that connect students with financial planning professionals, firms, and community partners.
* Mentor students and support their professional development through the Cofrin School of Business's "Transcripts to Résumés" initiative.
* Develop and maintain a productive program of scholarship consistent with rank, including opportunities for collaboration with students and faculty.
* Engage meaningfully with the financial planning profession, regional business community, and relevant professional organizations.
* Perform institutional and community service.
* Contribute to ongoing program development within the Austin E. Cofrin School of Business.
* Participate fully in the Austin E. Cofrin School of Business’ AACSB accreditation efforts.

**Start Date:**
---------------

August 23, 2027  



  

**Department:**
---------------

Accounting \& Finance  



  

**Compensation:**
-----------------

Competitive compensation commensurate with qualifications and experience.  



  

This position is exempt from the overtime provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).  



  

**Required Qualifications:**
----------------------------

* Earned doctorate in Personal Financial Planning, Finance, or Business with a specialization in Finance from an institution supporting an AACSB accredited business school by the end of the first academic year. Candidates who have not completed their doctorate by the start date will be hired into a terminal appointment at the rank of Instructor with a rate determined at the time of hire. Upon degree conferral, the title will change to Assistant Professor. The contract will not be renewed if the degree is not conferred by the end of the terminal appointment.
* Evidence of a commitment to quality teaching
* An ongoing record of scholarship, including peer\-reviewed journal publications, consistent with the level of experience
* CFP certification, or ability to sit for the CFP Board’s CFP® Certification Examination by the end of the second academic year
Evidence of engagement in institutional, community, and professional endeavors  
* 

  

**Conditions of Appointment:**
------------------------------

The home campus of this position is Green Bay. Courses will be taught both face\-to\-face and online (in asynchronous and synchronous formats). The specific courses taught may vary from semester to semester.  



  

Position is an academic year, tenure\-track appointment. Applicants must be considered for tenure and promotion in six years, although tenure decisions may be at any time. Promotion from Assistant to Associate Professor is simultaneous with tenure. Excellence in teaching, sustained scholarly activity, and institutional service required for retention and promotion. A pre\-employment education check which includes, but is not limited to, the verification of academic credentials will be conducted on the finalist(s). A criminal conviction investigation will be conducted on the finalist(s). In compliance with the Wisconsin Fair Employment Act, the university does not discriminate on the basis of arrest or conviction record. In addition, if the final selected candidate has prior work history within the last 7 years with Universities of Wisconsin, a personnel file review check for employee misconduct will be completed.

-----------------

Click the Apply button and follow the prompts on the screen.  



  

Please be sure to complete all required fields, and include all required documents before submitting your application. Once submitted, you will not be able to edit or attach any application materials. Files must be complete to be considered. Please include the following documents:


* Cover letter specifically addressing qualifications for the essential job functions
* Curriculum Vitae
Course Evaluations (when available)  
*

Human Resources

**The Successful Candidate**

In addition, the successful candidate will have strong oral, written, interpersonal, and organizational skills, demonstrated integrity and strong leadership, and the willingness to work independently and as part of a collaborative team. Our benefits package also includes dental, vision, several life insurance options, AD\&D and Accident insurance and Flexible Spending and Health Savings Accounts. * Support curriculum development and educational initiatives.

* Contribute to academic publications and educational materials.

**Administrative And Service Responsibilities**

**Job Description**
===================

**Position Summary:**
---------------------

The Department of Mathematics at Colorado State University invites applications for one tenure\-track assistant professor position in the area of Applied and Computational Mathematics with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027\. A broad range of application areas will be considered. Candidates should have an established research program, a compelling plan for future research, the ability to supervise both graduate and undergraduate research, and a record of excellence in teaching. The salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience, and includes a full benefits package.  



  

The Department of Mathematics at Colorado State University is one of eight departments in the College of Natural Sciences. The Department has a strong commitment to undergraduate and graduate teaching, as well as excellence in research. Faculty research interests include algebra, analysis, combinatorics, differential equations, geometry, inverse problems, math education, mathematical modeling, number theory, scientific computing, and topology, as well as applications of these areas. The Department of Mathematics has around 150 undergraduate majors and 73 graduate students, with currently 30 tenured and tenure\-track faculty.  



  

Work authorization visa sponsorship **may** be available based on the specific situation, including cost, for the selected final candidate.  



  

**Full Consideration Date: Friday, November 6, 2026, 11:59 pm (MT)**
--------------------------------------------------------------------

**Essential Job Duties:**
-------------------------

* Teach and mentor students at the undergraduate and graduate levels, including course and curriculum development.
* Conduct and publish research, pursue external funding, and contribute to scholarly advancement in the field.
Provide service to the department, university, profession, and community in support of CSU’s mission.  
* 

**Supervision:**
----------------

This position does not have direct reports.  

* 

  

**Conditions of Employment:**
-----------------------------

Pre\-employment Criminal Background Check (required for all new hires).  

* 

  

**Minimum Qualifications:**
---------------------------

* Terminal degree (Ph.D. or equivalent) in Mathematics or related area by application deadline.
* Evidence of research productivity or strong potential to establish a sustainable scholarly program (e.g., publications, presentations, grant activity).
* Demonstrated ability to teach effectively at the undergraduate and/or graduate level.

**Preferred Qualifications:**
-----------------------------

* Evidence of scholarly research in Applied and Computational Mathematics.
Evidence of teaching skills that show the candidate is prepared for teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels.  
* 

**Application Instructions:**
-----------------------------

**Please read the following instructions carefully and submit all required application materials.**

To apply, please **upload one single PDF containing all required application materials listed below, in the order provided.** Your materials should clearly outline your work experience, education, and other relevant qualifications and demonstrate how your background aligns with the required and preferred qualifications outlined in the posting. The required application materials include:


* A cover letter that addresses specific interests in CSU and its Department of Mathematics;
* A complete curriculum vitae;
* A teaching statement, limited to 2\-3 pages;
A research statement, limited to 2\-3 pages (references do not count towards the page limit).  
* 

  

**Important:** The single PDF containing all application materials must be uploaded under the section labeled **“Resume/CL.”** Please combine all materials into one PDF and ensure they are included in the specified order. You will not be able to modify or add documents after submitting your application, so please carefully review your materials before submitting. **Failure to submit the required materials as instructed may affect consideration of your application.**  



After submitting your application, you will receive an email with instructions to provide the contact information for **three professional references** . To help avoid delays in the search process, please complete this step as soon as possible.  



Once you submit your references’ contact information, each reference will receive an email with instructions for submitting a letter of recommendation. Letters of recommendation must be received by **November 13, 2026 (one week after full consideration date).**

**Please note:** For semi\-finalist candidates, submitted letters of recommendation, along with application materials, will be made available to the faculty of the Department of Mathematics for review.  



  

Please direct questions about the application process to Karena Alons, at karena.alons@colostate.edu.

$93,000\-$103,000

As a comprehensive institution of the University System of Georgia, Valdosta State University (VSU) is a welcoming, aware, and vibrant community founded on and dedicated to serving our communities' rich and diverse heritages. As members of this community and proud Blazers we strive to uphold these core values for the advancement of the University, as stated in the Blazer Creed and reflected in our commitment to the University System of Georgia's Core Values.


**Blazer Creed**


Valdosta State University is a learning environment based on trust and mutual respect in which open dialogue, vigorous debate, and the free exchange of ideas are welcome. The University is equally dedicated to the core values of community, including a commitment to practice **civility, integrity,** and **citizenship.** As members of this community, and proud Blazers, we will strive to uphold these core values for the advancement of the University.

**Citizenship** \- Every Blazer has an interest in the well\-being of the community, and, therefore, a duty to stay informed, to make positive contributions, and to offer support to those who need help.

The selected candidate will be responsible for teaching courses in the candidate's area of expertise, maintaining scholarly productivity, and participating in service at the department, college, and university levels.


The Langdale College of Business Administration programs are accredited by AACSB, placing the College among the top 5% of business colleges worldwide. The faculty in the Department of Management and Marketing cultivates a learning environment that emphasizes experiential learning, fosters critical thinking, and equips students with the creative and analytical abilities necessary for career success. Therefore, our primary emphasis is recruiting faculty members who uphold this exceptional level of excellence in teaching and whose research is characterized by novelty and applicability.

jobs.title: Alvin I. Goodman Chair, Nephrology
jobs.description:
**Overview**
 The Alvin I. Goodman Chair in Nephrology ("Goodman Chair") is an endowed position in the Department of Medicine at New York Medical College (NYMC) School of Medicine (SOM) for a physician scientist with specialization in nephrology, kidney transplantation, kidney biology, renal injury and repair, translational immunology, and/or closely related disciplines. Candidates for the position shall hold and/or be eligible for an NYMC SOM faculty appointment at the rank of professor, and shall be eligible for clinical appointment to the medical staff at Westchester Medical Center (WMC), the primary academic clinical affiliate of NYMC. The Goodman Chair is expected to build a nationally recognized, externally funded translational research program that advances kidney science, discovery, and academic nephrology as relates to their area(s) of specialization. The endowment opportunity provides funds, with appropriate approvals, to support the compensation of the holder of the Goodman Chair, as well as research and teaching activities conducted under the holder’s.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
* Develops, leads, and sustains a nationally recognized translational research program in nephrology, or closely related disciplines/ areas of study, such as transplantation biology, renal injury and repair, epithelial and/or endothelial biology, translational immunology, etc.
* Secures, maintains, and expands extramural research support from federal agencies, foundations, industry partners, philanthropy, and other mission\-aligned sources to support investigator\-initiated science, collaborative programs, research infrastructure, trainee development, and endowed chair activities.
* Leads development of competitive grant applications, program\-project proposals, center\-level initiatives, industry\-sponsored and investigator\-initiated studies, philanthropic proposals, and endowment opportunities that advance NYMC and WMC priorities in kidney disease, transplantation, and translational biology.
* Demonstrates sustained scholarly and research productivity through peer\-reviewed publications, national and international presentations, collaborative grants, trainee mentorship, and scientific leadership.
* Is expected to achieve a defined level of research productivity and financial sustainability within the first five years of appointment, including a substantial portfolio of investigator\-initiated extramural funding sufficient to support the Chair holder’s research program, key research personnel, and ongoing scholarly activity.
* Builds collaborative research programs across the academic health center including the WMCHealth network, basic science and clinical departments, and external partners with priority to advance kidney disease, transplantation, dialysis, and vascular/endothelial biology research.
* Provides academic leadership for research and teaching activities supported by endowment funds, ensuring that resources are used for NYMC\-approved research, educational, and scholarly activities conducted under the Chair holder’s direction.
* Mentors faculty, fellows, residents, medical students, graduate students, postdoctoral trainees, and research staff, with emphasis on career development, grant preparation, responsible conduct of research, and team\-based translational science.
* Participates in NYMC and WMC clinical faculty activities appropriate to expertise, including consultation, program development, academic conferences, and collaboration with nephrology, transplantation, critical care, and related clinical programs.
* Engages in teaching within the SOM, Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences, fellowship programs, and other NYMC educational programs as requested by the Department Chair and consistent with the Chair holder’s expertise.
* Adheres to all applicable federal, state, institutional, and sponsor requirements governing human subjects research, animal research, biosafety, data integrity, research compliance, reporting, and data sharing.
* Represents NYMC and WMC in regional, national, and international forums related to academic nephrology and/or closely related disciplines.
* Maintains continued eligibility for the Goodman Chair through sustained academic productivity, responsible stewardship of endowed resources, compliance with applicable policies and gift terms, active alignment with the endowed chair purpose, and satisfactory periodic review by the Department Chair and Dean of the SOM.


**Endowed Chair Stewardship Expectations**
* Develops, within the first year of appointment, a written five\-year research, funding, recruitment, and program\-development plan aligned with NYMC priorities, WMC clinical and translational missions, and the donor intent of the endowment.
* Uses endowed resources responsibly and transparently for allowable NYMC\-approved purposes, including salary support where permitted, research personnel, trainees, pilot studies, core services, equipment, grant development, scholarly travel, academic programming, and research or teaching activities conducted under the Chair holder’s direction.
* Partners with NYMC, WMC, WMCHealth, and institutional advancement or philanthropy leadership to cultivate federal, foundation, industry, philanthropic, and continued endowment support for academic nephrology, kidney science and related work.
* Participates in donor stewardship, philanthropic engagement, public\-facing academic presentations, investiture or recognition activities, and annual reporting that demonstrates the academic, scientific, educational, and clinical impact of the endowed chair.
* Provides an annual endowed chair impact report summarizing grants submitted and awarded, publications, invited presentations, trainees and junior faculty mentored, research staff supported, collaborations developed, philanthropy\-related activities, use of endowed funds, and progress toward five\-year goals.
* Builds a sustainable, cross\-cutting translational research enterprise that extends beyond a single disease or organ system while maintaining strong relevance to kidney disease and transplantation. The program may include investigator\-initiated clinical or translational studies, collaborative laboratory programs, research cores, biorepositories, data resources, pilot funding mechanisms, and interdisciplinary partnerships spanning immunology, inflammation, tissue injury and repair, epithelial and endothelial biology, vascular biology, critical care, surgery, pathology, nephrology, transplantation, and basic science programs.
* Develops a pipeline of physician\-scientists, translational investigators, and multidisciplinary research teams whose work bridges nephrology, transplantation, immunology, vascular biology, tissue injury and repair, and other cross\-cutting domains by mentoring students, trainees, staff and faculty toward independent funding and scholarly productivity.


**Qualifications**
* D., M.D./Ph.D. or equivalent degree.
* Board certification or eligibility in nephrology or a closely related discipline is expected.
* Eligible for faculty appointment at professor rank in the Department of Medicine.
* Eligible for New York State medical licensure and credentialing at Westchester Medical Center.
* Eligible for appointment to the medical staff of WMC.
* Computer literacy in PC and Mac\-based software applications including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and MS Office Suite; other software specific to research specialization, as needed.
* Established record as a senior academic physician\-scientist or translational investigator in nephrology, transplantation, immunology, kidney injury/repair, epithelial or endothelial biology, or related fields.
* Demonstrated history of extramural funding, high\-impact scholarship, program building, interdisciplinary collaboration, and mentorship of trainees and faculty required.
* Internationally or nationally recognized expertise in nephrology, transplantation biology, renal injury/repair, translational immunology, epithelial biology, endothelial biology, or related scientific domains.
* Demonstrated success securing extramural research support and leading productive, collaborative, and compliant research programs.
* Documented capacity to generate and sustain investigator\-initiated funding from federal, foundation, industry, philanthropic, and endowment\-related sources.
* Ability to prepare and execute a strategic plans addressing research, funding, recruitment, and sustainability plan with measurable milestones for grants, publications, mentorship, program development, and responsible use of endowed chair resources.
* Experience with donor stewardship, advancement partnerships, annual impact reporting, research compliance, grant administration, and transparent stewardship of restricted or endowed funds preferred.
* Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills with ability to engage faculty, trainees, hospital leadership, research administration, philanthropy, donors, industry partners, and external scientific collaborators.
* Strong leadership, mentoring, planning, and organizational skills in an academic health center environment.
* Ability to develop research infrastructure, recruit and retain research staff, manage start\-up resources in alignment with institutional mission and endowed purpose.
* Commitment to education, mentorship, academic citizenship, research integrity, professionalism, inclusive and engaging work ethic and ethical conduct.
* Ability to work cooperatively within the academic health center as well as external partners.
* Academic health center; clinical patient\-centered facilities, research labs, office, and teaching environments.
* Activities may include meetings, teaching sessions, clinical collaboration, laboratory/ research oversight, and occasional travel for scientific meetings.
* Standard academic health center, research, and clinical environments; must comply with institutional safety, biosafety, clinical, and research compliance requirements.


**Minimum Salary**
 USD $350,000\.00/Yr.
   

  

**Maximum Salary**

jobs.description:
#### **Description**


The McCombs School of Business at The University of Texas at Austin invites applications for a faculty position in Artificial Intelligence and Operations Management, beginning in Fall 2027\. We seek candidates with a strong commitment to high\-quality research and teaching who can contribute to our undergraduate and graduate courses in Artificial Intelligence and Operations Management. We are particularly interested in candidates who use rigorous empirical and data\-driven methods to address problems in application domains such as revenue management, supply chains, healthcare, retailing, transportation and logistics, and technology and operations.


A successful candidate will be expected to establish an internationally recognized research program at The University of Texas at Austin, mentor graduate students, and teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels. The predominant mode of instruction and research is in person; accordingly, faculty appointed for employment shall reside in the proximate area of the work site for the duration of their appointment and be able to maintain a daily in\-person schedule at the assigned work site.


The McCombs School of Business, with its top\-ranked faculty and educational programs, offers a stimulating and collegial environment for innovative research and teaching. The school’s research centers, including centers focused on supply chain management, electronic commerce, entrepreneurship, marketing, and energy management, provide opportunities to collaborate with colleagues across disciplines and interact with a range of industry partners in Austin, throughout Texas, and nationally.


A background check will be conducted on applicants selected for the position prior to appointment.


#### **Qualifications**


A Ph.D. (or very near completion) from an accredited institution is required by the start date of the appointment.


#### **Application Instructions**


Applicants should submit a letter of interest, curriculum vitae, a job\-market paper or other representative research manuscript, and a statement of research objectives and accomplishments. Three confidential letters of recommendation should also be submitted via Interfolio. Candidates with teaching experience should upload teaching evaluations.


At their discretion, applicants with prior faculty experience, such as current assistant or associate professors, may defer submission of recommendation letters during the initial application stage. Such candidates will be asked to provide references if selected as finalists. Additional materials may also be requested after the initial review of applications.


All materials should be submitted through Interfolio using the following link: apply.interfolio.com/194218


The application deadline is December 1, 2026\. Applications received by October 15, 2026, will also be considered for interviews at the INFORMS Annual Meeting on November 1, 2026\.


Please do not submit applications or updated materials via email.


#### **Equal Employment Opportunity Statement**


*The University of Texas at Austin, as an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer, complies with all applicable federal and state laws regarding nondiscrimination and affirmative action. The University is committed to a policy of equal opportunity for all persons and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability, religion, or veteran status in employment, educational programs and activities, and admissions.*

jobs.description:
The Department of Medicine and Section of Palliative Care in the Division of General Internal Medicine is seeking a full\-time physician (MD/DO), PhD scientist or PharmD in a relevant field with a research focus on palliative care and serious illness at the levels of Assistant Professor, appointment or tenure stream, Associate Professor, appointment or tenure stream and Professor, appointment stream or tenured depending on qualifications and career track to serve as the Associate Chief of Research (ACR) and Director of the Palliative Research Center (PaRC). In this role, the ACR will collaborate closely with the Section Faculty and report directly to the Section Chief.
   

  

 The Section of Palliative Care is a multidisciplinary team committed to improving quality of life for patients and families through delivery of quality palliative care, education of palliative care skills and advancement in palliative care innovation. We work with patients at academic hospitals and at outpatient clinics throughout the region. Our fellowship program is nationally recognized and comprised of four fellowship tracks to accommodate diverse career goals.
   

  

 The Palliative Research Center (PaRC) consists of faculty from across the Schools of Health Sciences, including researchers from palliative care and many medical subdisciplines, nursing, and public health. PaRC supports researchers throughout their careers and encourages collaboration between faculty members across disciplines.
   

  

**Key Responsibilities**
* Research Leadership – Develop and implement the strategic research mission of the Section and the Palliative Research Center (PaRC).
* Recruitment and Mentorship – Recruit junior and mid\-level investigators and provide mentorship for palliative care investigators.
* Collaboration and Engagement – Promote synergy and partnerships across disciplines and University departments, schools and institutes.
* Grant Funding – Nurture collaborative relationships with foundations and industries and advance federal research projects (NIH, PCORI).


**Resources Available**
* Palliative Research Center (PaRC)
* Center for Research on Health Care (CRHC)
* VA Center for Health Care Evaluation, Research Promotion (CHERP)
* Institute for Clinical Research Education (ICRE)


 Applicants for Assistant Professor, appointment or tenure stream, should have three or more years of experience in the field of clinical and/or health services research; have achieved or established the ability to attain external research funding; have dispersed results through peer\-reviewed publications and other scientific forums; have noteworthy teaching experience; and established the capability for continued career development, promotion, and tenure.
   

  

 Applicants for Associate Professor, appointment or tenure stream, should have five or more years of experience in the field of clinical and/or health services research; have independent, external research funding and an extensive record of peer\-reviewed publications; have substantial teaching experience; and demonstrate the ability for continued, impactful, independent scholarly contributions and leadership.
   

  

 Applicants for Professor, appointment stream or tenured, will have served five to seven years as Associate Professor. The rank of professor regards the individual accomplishments of respected knowledge and status in a distinguished ﬁeld of learning and the achievement of successful teaching knowledge and practices. The professor should have obtained enhanced stature in their ﬁeld through contributions of scholarship, professional practice, and leadership in professional and learning organizations.
   

  

 We offer a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and a dynamic working environment.
   

  

 Interested applicants should submit a curriculum vitae and apply to requisition number 26004568 via: https://www.join.pitt.edu.
   

  

 The University of Pittsburgh is an equal opportunity employer/disability/veteran.
